post_title: Communities Urged to Prepare Schools for 2026 Reopening
post_content:
n

As the New Year begins, the Mpumalanga Department of Education has called on communities to start preparations to ensure a smooth and successful reopening of schools for the 2026 academic year.

nnnn

The call follows persistent rainfall experienced across the province since the closure of schools in December 2025, which may have affected school infrastructure and surroundings. The Department has urged schools to take proactive steps to ensure that learning environments are safe, clean and ready for the return of learners and educators.

nnnn

Schools have been advised to prioritise activities such as cutting overgrown grass, trimming trees, rearranging flower beds, attending to vegetable gardens, cleaning and organising classrooms, and ensuring that all learning spaces are orderly and conducive to teaching and learning.

nnnn

The Department has further encouraged School Governing Bodies (SGBs), parents, community members and relevant stakeholders to work together and lead these efforts. This collective responsibility, it said, is essential to ensuring that teaching and learning begin without disruption from the first period on the day schools reopen.

nnnn

Meanwhile, Mpumalanga MEC for Education, Ms Lindi Masina, is set to officially launch the 2026 Back-to-School Campaign on Tuesday, 6 January 2026, at Mathupa Primary School in Marite, within the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality.

nnnn

The Back-to-School Campaign aligns with the Rhandza Xikolo Xa Wena Campaign, which aims to mobilise communities to take ownership of their schools and ensure that every learner returns to an environment that is safe, caring and fully prepared to deliver quality education.

nnnn

The Department has extended its best wishes for a prosperous and successful 2026 school year to learners, educators, school management teams, support staff, parents and education partners.

nnnn

“Together, let us make 2026 a year of commitment, excellence and shared responsibility in the Place of the Rising Sun,” the Department said.

post_title: Persistent Rains Endanger Provincial Roads
post_content:
n

Persistent heavy rainfall across parts of Mpumalanga continues to pose a serious threat to road safety, prompting the provincial Department of Public Works, Roads and Transport to urge motorists to exercise extreme caution when travelling.

nnnn

According to the Department, continuous rainfall has significantly affected road conditions in several areas, resulting in slippery surfaces, flooded low-lying areas, collapsed culvert bridges and damage to sections of the provincial road network. These conditions increase the risk of accidents, particularly if motorists fail to adapt their driving behaviour.

nnnn

MEC for Public Works, Roads and Transport, Mr Thomo, appealed to road users to prioritise safety at all times.

nnnn

“The persistent rainfall we are experiencing in parts of the province requires all road users to be extra vigilant. We are appealing to motorists to reduce speed, maintain a safe following distance and strictly obey the rules of the road. Reckless driving under these conditions puts lives at risk, and we cannot afford to lose more lives on our roads,” he said.

nnnn

The Department also cautioned that some road construction projects may experience temporary disruptions, as certain contractors are currently on festive season recess. Motorists have been urged to remain patient, adhere to road signage and respect temporary traffic control measures in areas under construction or repair.

nnnn

Several roads have been closed due to unsafe conditions. These include the R533 between Graskop and Bushbuckridge, the D481 between Ekulindeni and Mooiplaas, and the D1604 in Mbombela. The closures will remain in place until further notice.

nnnnnnnnnnnnnnnn

The Department confirmed that it remains on high alert and is closely monitoring road conditions across the province in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to ensure the safety of all road users.

nnnn

Motorists are encouraged to stay informed, plan their journeys carefully and avoid travelling through affected areas where possible.

post_title: Torrential Rains Impact Municipalities Across Region
post_content:
n

Bushbuckridge Local Municipality continues to closely monitor the impact of ongoing torrential rains affecting various parts of Mpumalanga, while disaster management teams remain on high alert to ensure the safety of communities.

nnnn

In neighbouring Thaba Chweu Local Municipality, no serious damage has been reported to date. However, the road between Graskop and Bushbuckridge has been closed as a safety precaution due to hazardous conditions caused by persistent rainfall.

nnnn

Within Bushbuckridge Local Municipality, damage has been recorded at Thabokgolo Primary School, where strong winds blew away the roof of the school’s office block. In addition, 11 households were affected by the severe weather. The affected families have since received assistance, while damage assessments are still ongoing to determine the full extent of the impact.

nnnn

Nkomazi Local Municipality has, so far, not reported any serious damage. Nevertheless, residents living near the Driekoppies Dam have been placed on alert after the dam reached 104 per cent capacity. Authorities have indicated that the opening of the sluice gates may be required later this evening, depending on water levels.

nnnn

The City of Mbombela has also been affected by the heavy rains. In Ward 43, at the Louisville-Kamashayana informal settlement, 64 households have been provided with relief material. Damage assessments are continuing, with a detailed report expected on Monday. In Ward 29, Pienaar, approximately 150 houses have been affected, and disaster management teams are on the ground delivering relief and conducting assessments. Meanwhile, in Ward 18 at Entokozweni, about 18 houses have already been assessed, with further evaluations underway.

nnnn

Residents are urged to remain vigilant and adhere to safety warnings as heavy rainfall continues across the region.

post_title: Masina Assures School Placement for All
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga MEC for Education, Ms Linda Masina, on Tuesday 6 January 2026 launched the 2026 Back to School Campaign at Mathupa Primary School in Marite, reaffirming the department’s commitment to ensuring that every learner is placed in a school by the end of January.

nnnn

Addressing parents, guardians and community members, MEC Masina acknowledged that while not all learners may be placed by the official reopening date of 14 January, the department is working to ensure that no child is left behind. To date, more than 1.3 million learners have been successfully placed across the province, with approximately 9 826 learners still awaiting placement.

nnnn

The department has established a dedicated help desk to assist parents with placement queries and appeals, as part of efforts to streamline the process and reduce anxiety ahead of the new academic year.

nnnn

As part of measures to address overcrowding and infrastructure challenges, the Mpumalanga Department of Education has procured 130 mobile classrooms. These will be deployed to schools experiencing high learner numbers, particularly in areas under pressure due to migration to urban centres.

nnnn

MEC Masina also announced that furniture has been secured for 342 schools across the province. In addition, the department has committed to repairing damages caused by recent floods before schools reopen on 14 January. Where extensive damage has occurred, assessments will be conducted, but alternative arrangements will be made to ensure that teaching and learning continue uninterrupted.

nnnn

“Our wish for 2026 is that it should be the year of growth, academic progress, safety and success for every learner and household in the province,” said Masina.

nnnn

She further called on parents and communities to play an active role in supporting education and creating safe, supportive environments for learners.

nnnn

The launch event also saw private sector support, with Old Mutual donating 50 pairs of school shoes to learners at Mathupa Primary School, adding a boost to the back-to-school drive in the Bushbuckridge area.

post_title: Compliance Urged for Learner Transport Safety
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga MEC for Public Works, Roads and Transport, Mr Thulasizwe Thomo, has called on all scholar transport operators in the province to ensure their vehicles are fully roadworthy and legally compliant ahead of the reopening of schools next week.

nnnn

With thousands of learners expected to return to classrooms following the festive recess, MEC Thomo stressed that learner safety must remain the top priority for everyone involved in scholar transport services.

nnnn

He urged operators to take full responsibility by ensuring vehicles are mechanically sound, properly licensed and driven by qualified, sober and responsible drivers. “Learner safety cannot be compromised. Operators must ensure that every vehicle transporting children meets all legal and safety requirements,” said Thomo.

nnnn

The MEC highlighted that vehicles used for scholar transport must undergo thorough inspections, including checks on brakes, tyres and steering systems, in accordance with the National Road Traffic Act and related regulations.

nnnn

He further warned that the Transport Inspectorate will intensify compliance monitoring across Mpumalanga, with a specific focus on scholar transport vehicles. Operators found to be in violation of the law will face firm action, including fines, the impoundment of vehicles and possible suspension of operating permits.

nnnn

“We will not hesitate to act against operators who put the lives of our children at risk. Learners deserve to be transported in safe and reliable vehicles every day,” he added.

nnnn

The department also appealed to parents, school management teams and community members to report unsafe scholar transport vehicles to the relevant authorities to help safeguard learners as the new school term begins.

post_title: Truck Driver Shot Dead in Bushbuckridge
post_content:
n

Police in Bushbuckridge have launched a manhunt following the fatal shooting of a truck driver along the R40 road at Dwarsloop earlier this week.

nnnn

The incident occurred on Tuesday night, 6 January 2026, at around 23:40, when police responded to a complaint about a truck that was suspiciously and incorrectly parked along the route. Upon arrival at the scene, officers discovered a man lying on the ground outside the truck with a gunshot wound to the head.

nnnn

Emergency medical services were called to the scene and declared the man dead on arrival.

nnnn

The truck owner was later contacted and identified the deceased as Mr Scelo Sphephelo Nxumalo (41), who was the driver of the vehicle.

nnnn

Police said the motive for the murder is still unknown, and no arrests have been made at this stage. The suspects remain at large, and investigations are continuing. It has also been confirmed that the truck was fitted with cameras, and footage from these devices is being analysed as part of the investigation.

nnnn

The South African Police Service has appealed to members of the public to assist with information that may lead to the arrest of those responsible. Anyone with relevant information is urged to contact the investigating officer, Detective Lieutenant Colonel Cindy Mkhabela, on 082 469 1298, call Crime Stop on 08600 10111, or submit a tip via the MySAPS App. All information will be treated with strict confidentiality, and anonymity is guaranteed.

nnnn

Police have also asked community members to come forward if they recognise a man shown in a photograph linked to the investigation, as this may assist in tracing the suspects.

nnnn

The incident has raised concerns about safety along major transport routes in the area, as investigations continue.

post_title: Illegal Immigrants, Traffickers Arrested

The South African Police Service (SAPS) in Mpumalanga has arrested twelve suspects during a crime prevention operation conducted in the Bushbuckridge policing area over the weekend.

nnnn

The operation, carried out under Operation Safer Festive Season by the former Acornhoek Cluster Crime Prevention Team, took place from 4pm on Friday, 10 January, until 4am on Saturday, 11 January 2026. It focused on preventing crime and disrupting serious and organised criminal activities.

nnnn

The arrests were made during stop-and-search operations along the R40 road in the Dwarsloop area. Police stopped and searched a taxi with Mozambican registration, leading to the apprehension of the suspects.

nnnn

Ten of the suspects were arrested for contravening South Africa’s Immigration Act and are believed to be undocumented foreign nationals from Mozambique. The remaining two suspects were arrested on charges related to human trafficking.

nnnn

Police also carried out extensive crime prevention activities across the wider Bushbuckridge area as part of the operation.

nnnn

Detectives are working closely with the Department of Home Affairs to verify the legal status of the arrested individuals. All twelve suspects are expected to appear before the Bushbuckridge Magistrate’s Court soon.

post_title: Pafuri, Giriyondo Posts Closed by Floods
post_content:
n

Two international border posts within the Kruger National Park have been temporarily closed following severe weather conditions affecting parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga.

nnnn

The Border Management Authority has confirmed the closure of the Pafuri and Giriyondo border posts after continuous heavy rainfall across the park, which follows a Level 6 severe weather warning issued for the region. Visitors have been urged to revise their travel plans and comply with guidance from park officials.

nnnn

Several rivers within the park are currently flowing at high speed, with water levels expected to rise further. These include the De Laporte, N’watshitsaka and Crocodile rivers. The Sabie River is also rising and is expected to impact the Sand River, which may disrupt travel routes between Satara Rest Camp, Tshokwane Picnic Site, Lower Sabie Rest Camp and Skukuza Rest Camp.

nnnnnnnn

Park management has cautioned that road closures may occur at short notice for safety reasons. Campers in affected areas will be relocated within camps, with those in caravans and motorhomes being moved closer to chalet zones. Visitors have also been advised not to remain in low-lying camping areas vulnerable to flooding.

nnnn

Guests travelling to Skukuza Airport from north of Tshokwane have been advised to use Kruger Gate via Satara or Orpen Gate, or alternatively access the airport from outside the park via the R40. Travellers are urged to allow extra time to avoid missing flights.

nnnn

Rainfall recorded overnight ranged from 25 mm in Phalaborwa to as high as 90 mm in Pafuri, with Tshokwane, Shingwedzi, Mooiplaas and Houtboschrand also recording significant rainfall.

nnnn

SANParks has strongly urged all visitors and staff to obey no-entry and road-closure signage, avoid flooded roads and low-lying bridges, and not to remove debris or barriers placed on roads.

nnnn

The South African Weather Service continues to monitor conditions and will issue updates as the situation evolves. The safety of visitors, staff and surrounding communities remains the park’s highest priority.

post_title: Recalled Infant Formula Raises Safety Concerns
post_content:
n

Parents and caregivers have been urged to stop using a specific infant formula following a national product recall linked to potential contamination that may pose a health risk to babies.

nnnn

The affected product is Nestlé NAN Special Pro HA Infant Formula (0–12 months), sold in an 800g can, with batch number 51660742F3 and a best-before date of 15 December 2026. The formula, which has been available on the South African market since September 2025, is intended for the dietary management of infants with allergies to cow’s milk.

nnnn

The recall follows the identification of a possible presence of cereulide, a toxin produced by the bacterium Bacillus cereus. Cereulide is considered a food safety concern and, if consumed, may cause symptoms such as severe or persistent vomiting, diarrhoea, or unusual lethargy, particularly in young infants.

nnnn

Health authorities have confirmed that the contamination has been traced back to a manufacturing facility in Germany that supplies several countries, including South Africa. Importantly, South Africa is reported to have received only this specific batch, and no other Nestlé products or batch numbers are affected by the recall.

nnnn

While no illnesses linked to the affected product have been confirmed locally, parents and caregivers are urged to remain vigilant. They are advised to monitor infants for any concerning symptoms and to consult a healthcare provider immediately if there are worries about a child’s health, even if symptoms are mild or absent.

nnnn

Consumers are encouraged to carefully check the batch number and best-before date on the product packaging. Anyone who has the recalled formula in their possession should return it to the place of purchase for a full refund.

nnnn

Authorities have emphasised that there is no need for panic, noting that precautionary measures are being taken in line with strict food safety and quality protocols. Ongoing engagement with relevant stakeholders is underway to ensure the protection of infant health.

nnnn

The recall has also renewed calls to support and promote breastfeeding as the optimal method of infant feeding. Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first six months of life, with continued breastfeeding up to two years or beyond alongside the gradual introduction of solid foods.

nnnn

Parents, caregivers and the public will continue to be informed of any developments related to the recall as more information becomes available.

post_title: Real Pass Rate Raises Alarm
post_content:
n

ActionSA has raised serious concerns about South Africa’s matric results, arguing that the widely celebrated 88% pass rate masks deep and ongoing failures within the basic education system.

nnnn

In a statement issued on 12 January 2026, ActionSA Parliamentary Chief Whip Lerato Ngobeni MP congratulated the Class of 2025 for completing their National Senior Certificate under challenging conditions, and acknowledged the role played by teachers and families. She said every learner who perseveres to the end of matric deserves recognition.

nnnn

However, ActionSA cautioned that headline pass rates do not present a full or honest picture of the system’s performance. Using a cohort-based analysis, which tracks how many learners who entered Grade 10 in 2023 eventually passed matric, the party calculates the effective pass rate at just 57.7%. This figure is based on the 1.14 million learners who began Grade 10, nearly half of whom did not successfully complete matric.

nnnn

According to ActionSA, this gap reflects a schooling system that continues to lose learners through dropout, repetition and disengagement long before they reach their final examinations. The party argues that success is being defined by reducing the number of learners who write matric, rather than by improving learning outcomes across the board.

nnnn

The party also highlighted ongoing safety and infrastructure challenges in schools. Ngobeni pointed to the recent death of a six-year-old girl in Nkuzana village, Limpopo, who fell into a pit toilet, despite such facilities being banned since 2013. A parliamentary reply last year revealed that about 590 schools across the country still rely on pit toilets, more than a decade after government committed to eradicating them.

nnnn

“A system that cannot guarantee basic safety and dignity for learners cannot credibly claim success based on pass percentages alone,” Ngobeni said.

nnnn

ActionSA reiterated its call for comprehensive education reform, including honest reporting of matric outcomes against full learner cohorts, the abolition of the 30% pass mark in favour of meaningful minimum standards, and structured academic support for learners who fall behind. The party also supports the reintroduction of Annual National Assessments and transparent school-level performance data to rebuild accountability.

nnnn

Looking ahead, ActionSA argues that South Africa needs an education system aligned with the realities of a modern economy. It has proposed a dual-stream education model from Grade 10, allowing learners to choose between academic and vocational pathways that respond to the country’s skills needs.

nnnn

“Our education system is not failing by accident,” Ngobeni said. “It is failing because leaders repeatedly choose political comfort over honest reform.” ActionSA says it will continue to push for higher standards, safer schools and an education system that prepares young South Africans not only to pass, but to thrive.

post_title: Flooded Access Route Cuts Off Wales Village
post_content:
n

Residents of Wales Village in Ward 32 have been left completely cut off from essential services after heavy rains caused the area’s only access route to flood, raising serious safety and humanitarian concerns.

nnnn

According to community members, the flooding has submerged a low-lying bridge that serves as the sole entry and exit point to the village. Residents say the situation is unprecedented, with water levels higher than those experienced during the severe floods of 2000.

nnnn

Although an assessment was previously conducted for the construction of a proper bridge, the process never progressed beyond that stage. In addition, residents were promised a tarred ring road during the 2019 election period, but no development has since taken place.

nnnn

As a result, the community is now isolated. In the event of a medical emergency, residents are unable to reach a clinic, hospital or mortuary. Community leaders warn that this lack of access places lives at immediate risk, as even minor illnesses or accidents could turn fatal due to delays in receiving help.

nnnn

The flooding also poses a serious danger to learners who must cross the affected route to attend school. With persistent rainfall, many children may be unable to travel safely, potentially disrupting their education and exposing them to further risk.

nnnn

Calls have been made for urgent intervention by the Department of Public Works, Roads and Transport to implement immediate temporary measures to restore safe access. Residents are also demanding that long-term solutions, including the construction of a proper bridge and the promised tarred road, be prioritised without further delay.

nnnn

Community members say reliable infrastructure is essential, not optional, and that no village should be left stranded whenever it rains. They are urging authorities to act swiftly to ensure safety, dignity and uninterrupted access to vital services for the people of Wales Village.

post_title: Mpumalanga Celebrates Strong Matric Results
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga has once again demonstrated its commitment to education after achieving an impressive 86.55% pass rate in the 2025 National Senior Certificate (NSC) examinations.

nnnn

Premier Mandla Ndlovu announced the results with pride, noting that the province improved on its 84.9% pass rate recorded in 2024. Mpumalanga’s performance also contributed to South Africa’s historic national matric pass rate of 88%.

nnnn

A standout success story from the province is Luyanda Ndlozi from Elangwana Secondary School, who emerged as Mpumalanga’s top achiever and ranked among the top 40 learners nationally. His achievement highlights the potential of learners in the province when given the necessary support and opportunities.

nnnn

Reflecting on the journey of the Class of 2025, Premier Ndlovu acknowledged the unique challenges they faced. “The Class of 2025 started high school during the COVID-19 pandemic, yet their commitment prevailed. Behind every success story stands a dedicated teacher, a parent who sacrificed, and a community that believed,” he said.

nnnn

In recognition of excellence and to further support education, the Mandla Ndlovu Foundation, in partnership with the Department of Education, donated full school uniforms to 1,000 learners across 10 top-performing schools that achieved a 100% pass rate.

nnnn

Premier Ndlovu emphasised that education remains central to the province’s development. “We see each successful matriculation as a step towards building a prosperous future—an era where education becomes the foundation for economic empowerment and social progress,” he said.

nnnn

The province extended its congratulations to the Class of 2025, encouraging learners to carry their success forward and continue making Mpumalanga proud.

post_title: Mass Arrests and Seizures in Mpumalanga
post_content:
n

A major law enforcement initiative, Operation Shanela II, has led to numerous arrests, seizures, and inspections across Mpumalanga. The operation, which ran from 8 to 11 January, involved the South African Police Service (SAPS), Traffic Police, law enforcement agencies, and several government departments, including Home Affairs, Health, and Correctional Services, alongside private security and community policing forums.

nnnn

During the operation, authorities conducted:

nnnn

• 72 premises searches and visits

nnnn

• 5 623 people and 1 789 vehicles screened

nnnn

• 1 258 patrols and 546 stop-and-searches

nnnn

• 101 vehicle checkpoints and 28 roadblocks

nnnn

• 3 240 patrols across the province

nnnn

• Tracing of 111 wanted suspects

nnnn

• Searches of 17 hostels

nnnn

Businesses and commercial operations were also inspected, with nine unlicensed liquor outlets closed, 240 licensed liquor outlets checked, 45 second-hand dealers inspected, and 578 informal businesses, including spaza shops, scrutinised for labour-law compliance. Additionally, 160 farms and 23 mines were visited.

nnnn

The operation resulted in arrests for a wide range of crimes, including:

nnnn

• 224 for assault with grievous bodily harm

nnnn

• 256 for driving under the influence

nnnn

• 186 for illegal liquor dealing

nnnn

• 51 for drug possession and 17 for drug dealing

nnnn

• 12 for murder and 28 for rape

nnnn

• 108 illegal immigrants detained

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi praised officers and stakeholders for their “dedication and professionalism,” while also thanking law-abiding community members for their support.

post_title: 33 Undocumented Children Intercepted at Beitbridge
post_content:
n

The Border Management Authority (BMA) has intercepted another group of undocumented minor children at the Beitbridge Port of Entry on Tuesday, 13 January 2026.

nnnn

According to the BMA, the interception took place at around 12:30 when a junior border guard, deployed during the relief shift, stopped and searched a Zimbabwe-registered minibus taxi at the port of entry. The vehicle was found to be transporting 33 undocumented children, aged between four and 15, who were travelling from South Africa to Zimbabwe.

nnnn

Two Zimbabwean men, aged 32 and 23, were arrested on suspicion of facilitating the illegal cross-border movement of the children. Criminal cases have been opened against the suspects under the Immigration Act for the facilitation of the illegal entry and movement of undocumented persons. They are expected to appear in court later this week.

nnnn

All 33 children were immediately handed over to the Department of Social Development for further processing, in accordance with child protection protocols and South Africa’s domestic and international obligations to safeguard vulnerable persons.

nnnn

The Commissioner of the Border Management Authority, Dr Michael Masiapato, praised the junior border guard for his vigilance and professionalism, saying the interception demonstrated the effectiveness of strengthened border controls. He also urged parents and guardians to refrain from sending undocumented children through ports of entry.

nnnn

“The Border Management Authority will not tolerate the exploitation of children or the facilitation of illegal cross-border movement. We remain committed to protecting the integrity of our borders while upholding human rights and child protection principles,” said Dr Masiapato.

nnnn

Investigations into the matter are continuing.

post_title: ANCYL Calls for Class Suspension Amid Floods
post_content:
n

The African National Congress Youth League (ANCYL) Ward 3 has issued an urgent call for the immediate suspension of classes at all schools in the Mkhuhlu Circuit following severe rainfall and flooding in the area.

nnnn

In a statement released this week, the ANCYL said heavy rains have caused significant damage to infrastructure, with several low-lying areas submerged. Roads, bridges and key access routes to schools have been affected, placing learners and educators at serious risk.

nnnn

“The safety, health and well-being of our learners must come first,” the organisation said, stressing that no compromise should be made when it comes to protecting children from potential danger.

nnnn

The ANCYL urged relevant authorities to act swiftly to assess the damage, repair affected infrastructure and implement proper safety measures before schools resume. It also called on parents, school management teams and government departments to work together to ensure learners are protected during the ongoing adverse weather conditions.

nnnn

“Our children’s lives matter more than anything,” the statement read.

nnnn

The call comes as several communities in the region continue to experience disruptions caused by flooding, with residents reporting difficulties in travelling and accessing essential services.

post_title: Mpumalanga Matric Class Praised
post_content:
n

ActionSA has congratulated the Mpumalanga Matric Class of 2025 for completing one of the most demanding milestones of their academic journey, describing their achievement as a testament to resilience, discipline and determination.

nnnn

In a statement released on Tuesday, ActionSA Member of the Mpumalanga Legislature Thoko Mashiane said the Class of 2025 had persevered under difficult circumstances, often in under-resourced schools, and deserved recognition for their efforts.

nnnn

Mpumalanga recorded an impressive provincial pass rate of 86.55%, contributing to South Africa’s historic national pass rate of 88% in 2025 – the highest ever recorded. Mashiane said the figures reflected not only academic performance but also the courage and commitment of learners who refused to be defined by their challenges.

nnnn

“Behind every result are learners who worked tirelessly, often in overcrowded classrooms and with limited resources, to achieve commendable outcomes,” she said. “Many attained strong marks that reflect potential and hard work.”

nnnn

The province also celebrated several outstanding individual performances. Siyanda Nkuna from Inkomazi High School was recognised as a national top achiever and an exceptional performer in mathematics. Angie Ntuli of Phumzile Secondary School was honoured among the top 40 learners nationally, while Luyanda Ndhlozi from Elangwane Secondary School in Volksrust emerged as Mpumalanga’s top learner, also ranking among the country’s top 40 performers.

nnnn

Mashiane said these achievements proved that excellence exists within the public education system and that Mpumalanga learners are able to compete with the best in the country when given the right support and opportunities.

nnnn

However, she cautioned that pass rate statistics should not mask the deep inequalities that continue to shape the education system. Persistent challenges such as inadequate infrastructure, uneven teaching support and overcrowded classrooms continue to limit many learners’ full potential.

nnnn

“A pass rate alone cannot capture the personal triumphs, resilience and effort behind these results,” she said.

nnnn

ActionSA called on government to move beyond announcements and implement targeted interventions in underperforming schools, invest meaningfully in teacher development and ensure equitable access to learning resources.

nnnn

Addressing the Class of 2025 directly, Mashiane said the journey did not end with matric results. “Whether you passed with distinction, achieved a solid pass or fell short of your goals, your effort matters. You have shown courage in the face of adversity, and South Africa needs that spirit as you take the next step in your lives.”

post_title: Mpumalanga Set for Mass FMD Vaccination Drive
post_content:
n

Parts of Mpumalanga will be prioritised in a nationwide mass vaccination programme aimed at containing the outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), Agriculture Minister John Steenhuisen has announced.

nnnn

Addressing the media at the GCIS Imbizo Centre in Cape Town, Steenhuisen said the Department of Agriculture would roll out an intensified vaccination campaign across all nine provinces to curb the spread of the highly contagious viral disease, which affects cloven-hoofed animals.

nnnn

FMD has now been confirmed in eight provinces, with the Northern Cape the only province yet to record any cases. Mpumalanga and Limpopo have been identified as high-risk areas due to recurring infections, particularly in regions where buffalo farming has expanded.

nnnn

According to Steenhuisen, the department has already vaccinated close to two million animals since the disease re-emerged in April last year. He said the new phase of interventions would focus on immediate mass vaccination in affected areas, followed by repeat vaccinations within three months.

nnnn

“In those provinces, we will see 100% vaccination of feedlots and dairy cows, 90% of commercial animals and 80% of communal livestock,” Steenhuisen said.

nnnn

He added that in hotspot areas such as parts of Mpumalanga, bi-annual vaccination campaigns would be introduced, especially along border zones where the risk of transmission remains high. Ongoing vaccination will also continue within designated protection zones.

nnnn

The minister emphasised that the programme is critical to protecting livestock, safeguarding livelihoods and stabilising the agricultural sector, particularly for small-scale and communal farmers who are most vulnerable to the economic impact of outbreaks.

nnnn

Local farmers in Mpumalanga are urged to cooperate with veterinary services and ensure their animals are presented for vaccination as the campaign is rolled out in the coming weeks.

post_title: Classes Suspended in Bushbuckridge Due to Heavy Rains
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Department of Education has announced the temporary suspension of classes in the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality following persistent heavy rainfall that has disrupted schooling in the area.

nnnn

In a statement issued on Wednesday, 14 January 2026, the department said it held an urgent meeting with District Directors and affected Circuit Managers to assess the impact of the ongoing weather conditions on teaching and learning across the province.

nnnn

The department noted that schools in the Nkangala and Gert Sibande districts have reopened smoothly, with teaching and learning commencing without major challenges. This, it said, has created a positive and focused environment for learners and educators in those areas.

nnnn

However, conditions in the Bohlabela District, particularly in Bushbuckridge, remain a cause for concern. Continuous rainfall has resulted in waterlogged and inaccessible roads, making it difficult for some learners and teachers to reach their schools safely.

nnnn

As a result, the department has decided to temporarily suspend classes in the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality for two days, from Thursday, 15 January to Friday, 16 January 2026.

nnnn

In the broader Ehlanzeni District, school principals have been granted the authority to use their discretion, based on on-the-ground assessments, to determine whether it is safe for schools to operate. This measure is aimed at ensuring the safety of both learners and staff.

nnnn

The department emphasised that the advisory allowing schools to exercise discretion remains in place for all areas currently affected by rainfall. However, due to the severity of conditions reported in Bushbuckridge, a full temporary suspension was deemed necessary.

nnnn

Community members have been urged to remain vigilant and to prioritise safety at all times. The department strongly appealed to residents not to attempt crossing flooded rivers, submerged bridges or unsafe roads under any circumstances.

nnnn

“The safety of our children is a shared responsibility,” the department said, adding that it will continue to closely monitor developments and provide updates as the situation evolves.

post_title: Bushbuckridge Music Community Mourns Sandile Mukasi
post_content:
n

The Bushbuckridge music fraternity is in mourning following the passing of Sandile Mukasi, affectionately known as Mama Cindy, a respected and much-loved figure within the local music community. She passed away on 12 January 2026, leaving behind a legacy of compassion, unity and unwavering support for local artists.

nnnn

Through her involvement with the Bushbuckridge Music Association (BUMA), Sandile Mukasi played a significant role in strengthening relationships within the music industry and supporting emerging talent across Bushbuckridge. She was widely regarded as a unifying force, always willing to lend a helping hand and advocate for the growth of the creative sector.

nnnn

In honour of her life and in solidarity with her family, BUMA has called on its members, as well as other music organisations in Bushbuckridge, to contribute R100 per member towards funeral and related financial arrangements. The association has further noted that any additional contribution, regardless of the amount, will be deeply appreciated and will assist the family during this difficult time.

nnnn

The funeral service will take place on 18 January 2026, with the time to be announced.

nnnn

As the community prepares to lay Sandile Mukasi to rest, musicians and cultural practitioners stand together in remembrance of a woman whose dedication and kindness left a lasting imprint on Bushbuckridge’s music landscape. Her spirit and contribution will continue to resonate through the work of the artists she supported.

post_title: Prospective Students Urged to Use Central Application Service
post_content:
n

Higher Education and Training Minister Buti Manamela has encouraged prospective students who need guidance in accessing the Post-School Education and Training (PSET) system to make use of the Central Application Service (CAS), as government rolls out reforms aimed at improving access and protecting learners.

nnnn

The Minister said the Department of Higher Education and Training had previously introduced the Central Applications Clearing House (CACH) as a short-term measure to match unplaced applicants with available study spaces. However, from the 2026 academic year, CACH will be discontinued as part of broader changes to the application process.

nnnn

According to Manamela, CAS has been developed as a comprehensive, long-term solution that integrates information across the entire PSET system. He said the service will progressively make visible a wider range of learning pathways beyond traditional universities and colleges, while also helping to eliminate bogus institutions and protect students from exploitation. Learners seeking information and guidance can WhatsApp the CAS Chat number on 081 308 4196.

nnnn

The department has also warned students and parents to be vigilant against illegal colleges that operate outside the law and offer unrecognised qualifications. Manamela stressed that qualifications offered by private skills development providers must be quality assured by recognised bodies, including the Quality Council for Trades and Occupations, relevant Sector Education and Training Authorities and the South African Qualifications Authority. He cautioned that bogus colleges often exploit periods of transition by charging fees without delivering credible outcomes, urging families to verify institutions on the department’s official platforms before making payments.

nnnn

Acknowledging that the move from school to further study can be emotionally demanding, the Minister said the department, through Higher Health, provides free and confidential psychosocial and mental health support. Students requiring assistance with stress, anxiety or crisis-related concerns can contact the 24-hour Higher Health Helpline on 0800 36 36 36.

nnnn

Manamela also announced expanded funding opportunities, noting that more than 15 000 SETA bursaries have been made available for students who do not qualify for National Student Financial Aid Scheme funding, particularly those in the “missing middle” and in scarce skills areas. The bursaries support studies at universities and TVET colleges and cover tuition, learning materials and other study-related costs.

nnnn

The department has advised students and parents to rely only on official communication channels, keep application records, and remain cautious of anyone claiming to guarantee placement or accommodation for a fee. Manamela encouraged learners who do not immediately receive offers to explore alternative pathways, emphasising that South Africa’s PSET system offers multiple entry points and second-chance opportunities for those willing to persist.

post_title: Disaster Looms as Level 10 Rainfall Warning Issued
post_content:
n

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Red Level 10 Warning for Disruptive Rainfall for parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga, warning that the risk of severe flooding remains critically high over the next 48 hours.

nnnn

According to SAWS, the warning follows several days of intense rainfall that has already saturated catchment areas, rivers and dams. With further heavy rain expected, authorities say the likelihood of widespread flooding has increased significantly, posing a serious threat to lives, livelihoods and infrastructure.

nnnn

SAWS cautions that potential impacts may include fast-flowing rivers and streams that could endanger lives, flooding of roads, bridges and low-lying crossings, and extensive damage to settlements, property and critical infrastructure. Communities may also face displacement, while essential services such as electricity, water supply and transport could be severely disrupted.

nnnn

Forecast guidance indicates that an additional 100 to 200 millimetres of rainfall may fall over parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga within the next 24 to 48 hours. Areas expected to be most affected include Maruleng and Ba-Phalaborwa Local Municipalities, Nkomazi Local Municipality, the City of Mbombela, Bushbuckridge Local Municipality, Greater Giyani, Greater Tzaneen, Greater Letaba and Collins Chabane.

nnnn

The Red Level 10 Warning will remain in effect for as long as conditions continue to pose a severe risk. Residents in affected areas are urged to remain vigilant, avoid travelling through flooded roads or bridges, and follow guidance from local authorities and disaster management teams.

nnnn

SAWS has advised communities to stay informed through official weather updates and emergency alerts as the situation continues to develop.

post_title: Severe Weather Forces Temporary Closure to Kruger Day Visitors
post_content:
n

Day visits to the Kruger National Park have been temporarily suspended as persistent heavy rainfall continues to affect parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga, raising safety concerns across the region.

nnnn

South African National Parks (SANParks) confirmed that the decision was taken as a precautionary measure in response to deteriorating weather and road conditions. The suspension will remain in place until conditions improve and is being reviewed on an ongoing basis.

nnnn

According to SANParks, the prolonged rainfall has placed considerable strain on operational and emergency response resources. The organisation said it is prioritising real emergencies and the safety of guests, staff and neighbouring communities, rather than risking avoidable incidents linked to non-essential travel within the park.

nnnn

“The safety of all visitors and staff remains our highest priority,” SANParks said, adding that the suspension of day visitors is intended to reduce risk during this period of severe weather.

nnnn

The impact of the heavy rains has already been felt within the park. Letaba Rest Camp is currently evacuating both staff and guests after floodwaters from the Letaba River entered the camp. In addition, Phalaborwa Gate has been closed for at least 24 hours while conditions are closely monitored. As a result, there is presently no access to the northern sections of the park.

nnnn

SANParks has apologised for the inconvenience caused by the ongoing rainfall and thanked the public for their understanding and cooperation. Further updates will be issued as the situation develops and as assessments of weather and road conditions continue.

nnnn

Visitors and community members are encouraged to stay informed through official SANParks communication channels while the severe weather persists.

post_title: Minster moves to scrap drinking and driving policy
post_content:
n

The Minister of Transport has announced plans to amend South Africa’s drinking and driving laws, declaring that any policy which allows motorists to consume alcohol before getting behind the wheel is no longer acceptable. The announcement was made during the release of the 2025/26 Festive Season Road Safety Campaign report.

nnnn

Presenting the report, the Minister revealed the scale of enforcement conducted over the festive season. A total of 1 632 roadblocks were carried out nationwide, with approximately 1.8 million vehicles stopped and checked. During this period, more than 450 000 traffic fines were issued, while 525 motorists were arrested for excessive speeding.

nnnn

Law-enforcement operations focused on roadworthiness, driver fitness and licensing. In addition, 173 695 drivers were tested for driving under the influence of alcohol. Of these, 8 561 tested positive — representing a 144 percent increase compared to the same period last year.

nnnn

The highest alcohol reading was recorded in KwaZulu-Natal, where one motorist tested at fourteen times above the legal alcohol limit. Meanwhile, the most extreme speeding incident occurred in the Northern Cape, where a driver was arrested after being clocked at 222 km/h in a 120 km/h zone. Officers also arrested 89 motorists for attempting to bribe traffic officials to avoid arrest.

nnnn

Beyond enforcement, the campaign placed strong emphasis on education and awareness. A total of 2 547 physical education and awareness programmes were conducted across the country, including outreach at mass transit departure points, shopping centres and other areas of high public activity. These efforts were supported by extensive awareness campaigns on radio, television and social media platforms.

nnnn

Encouragingly, preliminary annual statistics indicate a downward trend in road crashes and fatalities. In 2025, a total of 9 674 crashes resulted in 11 418 fatalities, compared to 10 633 crashes and 12 581 fatalities in 2021. Compared to 2024, crashes decreased by 6.4 percent, while fatalities declined by 6.2 percent — the lowest figures recorded in the past five years.

nnnn

The Minister thanked traffic officers at national, provincial and local government levels, as well as SAPS and emergency services, for their dedication throughout the year. Appreciation was also extended to provincial MECs, municipal MMCs for Transport, traditional authorities, and the organised bus, taxi and trucking sectors, alongside civil society organisations, for their role in reducing road accidents.

nnnn

Looking ahead, the Department will intensify consistent traffic law enforcement, particularly over weekends and public holidays, and will strengthen education and enforcement initiatives targeting pedestrians. The Minister noted that in towns, cities and rural areas, pedestrians account for roughly half of all road deaths.

nnnn

Describing road fatalities as “a reason for national shame”, the Minister stressed that deaths on the roads are neither inevitable nor unavoidable. Analysis shows that human behaviour — especially reckless driving — remains the leading cause of road trauma, with speeding and drunk driving the primary contributors.

nnnn

It was against this backdrop that the Minister confirmed plans to amend Section 65 of the National Road Traffic Act. The current drinking and driving policy, formulated nearly 30 years ago, allows drivers to consume limited amounts of alcohol before driving. The Minister stated that this law must be scrapped in favour of a clear and unambiguous rule: drinking and driving is not allowed.

nnnn

“If nothing else, we owe this to the memory of the many South Africans who have lost their lives on our roads,” the Minister said.

nnnn

nnnn

post_content:
n

Persistent rainfall continues to affect large parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga, forcing the temporary suspension of day visitation to the Kruger National Park (KNP) until further notice.

nnnn

Access to the park is now strictly limited to essential delivery vehicles, airport transfers with confirmed bookings, guests with existing overnight reservations at Berg en Dal, Pretoriuskop and Skukuza rest camps, and essential staff.

nnnn

The northern regions of the park remain inaccessible due to flooding and damaged roads. Satara Rest Camp has also been affected, with staff quarters submerged; affected staff were safely evacuated and no injuries have been reported. Water and electricity disruptions have led to the temporary closure of the camp.

nnnn

All tourism activities, including guided game drives and bush walks, are suspended as many internal roads remain unsafe. Visitors leaving the park are advised to monitor local road conditions, as flooding has impacted surrounding provincial and regional routes.

SANParks continues to work with disaster management authorities and urges the public to follow official channels for updates. Guest and staff safety remains the highest priority.

nnnnnnnn

post_title: DBE Urges Matric Second Chance Use
post_content:
n

The Department of Basic Education (DBE) has encouraged National Senior Certificate (NSC) candidates who were unsuccessful in their initial examination attempts to take advantage of the official Second Chance Matric Programme.

nnnn

The programme, which is provided free of charge, allows eligible candidates to rewrite or add subjects during the May/June examination cycle, in line with departmental policies. The DBE has emphasised that no payment is required to participate and has cautioned learners and parents against private or commercial services claiming to offer access to the programme for a fee.

nnnn

“The Department does not endorse any private or commercial services that require payment for participation in the Second Chance Programme,” the DBE said. “For authentic information, candidates are advised to contact the Department of Basic Education directly or visit the official website.”

nnnn

The Second Chance Matric Programme is designed to support learners who have not met the requirements of the NSC or the Extended Senior Certificate. It forms part of government’s broader efforts to improve access to education and increase learner retention, in line with the goals of the National Development Plan and the priorities of the basic education sector.

nnnn

Beyond providing a second opportunity to complete school qualifications, the programme also exposes learners to bursary opportunities for further studies, helping them to pursue post-school education and training pathways.

nnnn

The DBE outlined the categories of candidates who qualify for support under the programme. These include Senior Certificate Examination candidates who are registered to write the June examinations, as well as part-time NSC candidates who first attempted the NSC examinations after 2008 and will be writing in the May/June or November examination sessions.

nnnn

A range of key subjects is covered through the Second Chance Programme. These include Accounting, Agricultural Sciences, Business Studies, Economics, English First Additional Language, Geography, History, Mathematics, Mathematical Literacy, Physical Sciences and Life Sciences.

nnnn

Meanwhile, the DBE confirmed that the 2025 Matric Results will be released on 12 January 2026. More than 900 000 candidates sat for the 2025 examinations across approximately 7 000 examination centres nationwide. The process was supported by thousands of invigilators, as well as more than 51 000 markers and moderators, underscoring the scale of the national assessment effort.

nnnn

The department has reiterated its commitment to supporting learners to complete their schooling and has urged all eligible candidates to make use of the Second Chance Matric Programme to improve their results and future prospects.

post_title: Red Alert Issued As Flood Risk Persists
post_content:
n

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has confirmed that the Red Level 10 warning for disruptive rainfall remains in place for Friday across the Lowveld region of Mpumalanga, with communities in Nkomazi, Bushbuckridge and the City of Mbombela identified as the most affected areas.

nnnn

According to SAWS, residents should expect on-and-off showers and periods of persistent rain throughout the day. The ongoing rainfall is attributed to tropical moisture affecting the Lowveld and the escarpment areas of Mpumalanga, creating conditions that significantly increase the risk of flooding.

nnnn

SAWS has warned that the soil across much of the region is already saturated, heightening the likelihood of severe impacts. These include widespread flooding, fast-flowing streams and rivers, and potential danger to life. In some areas, flooding could lead to the displacement of communities and extensive damage to homes and other structures.

nnnn

The weather service further cautioned that there is a strong possibility of damage to property, buildings and essential infrastructure, with many residents facing the risk of losing livelihoods. Road infrastructure is also vulnerable, raising concerns that some communities may become inaccessible or cut off for prolonged periods as a result of damaged bridges and washed-away roads.

nnnn

Emergency services and local authorities are on high alert, and residents living in flood-prone areas have been urged to take extra precautions. SAWS has advised people to avoid crossing flooded roads and streams, to secure valuable belongings, and to relocate to safer areas if instructed to do so by authorities.

nnnn

Members of the public are strongly encouraged to remain vigilant and to stay informed by regularly monitoring official SAWS weather updates and warnings through trusted platforms, including radio, television and verified social media channels. Misinformation during severe weather events can place lives at risk, and residents are advised to rely only on official sources.

nnnn

SAWS has reiterated that it will continue to closely monitor the evolving weather system and will issue further updates as conditions change. Communities in the affected areas are urged to take the warnings seriously and to prioritise safety as heavy rainfall continues across the Lowveld.

post_title: Mpumalanga Needs R2.1 Billion For Flood Repairs Infrastructure
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga provincial government says it will require an estimated R2.1 billion to repair infrastructure damaged by recent heavy rains and flooding, with bridges and roads among the most severely affected.

nnnn

Persistent rainfall since late last year has caused widespread flooding across the province, washing away roads, damaging bridges and leaving some communities temporarily cut off from essential services. Provincial authorities say preliminary assessments indicate that the cost of repairing the damage is substantial and could increase as further evaluations are conducted.

nnnn

According to the provincial government, several bridges have been badly damaged or rendered unsafe, making them a top priority for repair. Bridges play a crucial role in connecting rural communities to schools, clinics, hospitals and markets, and their closure has disrupted daily life, emergency services and local economic activity.

nnnn

In addition to bridge damage, numerous roads have been affected by erosion, potholes and collapsing surfaces, while incidents such as rockfalls on key routes, including parts of the R38, have raised safety concerns for motorists.

nnnn

More than 1 200 households across Mpumalanga are reported to have been affected by the flooding, with some families displaced and others struggling with limited access to transport and basic services. Authorities have warned that rivers and dams remain under pressure, increasing the risk of further flooding should heavy rains continue.

nnnn

The scale of the damage has contributed to the national declaration of a disaster, allowing government to coordinate relief efforts and mobilise resources across affected provinces, including Mpumalanga and Limpopo.

nnnn

Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs Minister Velenkosini Hlabisa has assured the public that disaster relief funding will be closely monitored to ensure it reaches the communities most in need. The Mpumalanga government is expected to submit detailed damage reports to the National Disaster Management Centre as part of the process to access national funding.

nnnn

Provincial officials have emphasised that the R2.1 billion figure is a preliminary estimate, and that final costs will depend on further technical assessments and the extent of repairs required.

nnnn

Meanwhile, residents are urged to remain cautious, avoid damaged roads and bridges, and follow safety warnings issued by authorities as recovery and repair efforts continue.

post_title: Floods Test Kruger, SANParks Earns Minister’s Praise
post_content:
n

The Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, Mr Willie Aucamp, has commended South African National Parks (SANParks) for its “safety-first” approach following his visit to the flood-affected Kruger National Park.

nnnn

Minister Aucamp visited the park to assess damage caused by heavy rainfall and to engage with SANParks management and other stakeholders. Large parts of Mpumalanga and Limpopo have experienced severe weather over recent days, resulting in flooding and disruptions to infrastructure and park operations.

nnnn

“While there have been major disruptions and damage due to the heavy rains, it has been encouraging to witness the well-planned and coordinated response by Kruger National Park,” said Aucamp. “Early warning systems allowed emergency teams to act timeously and evacuate staff and guests safely.”

nnnn

The Minister praised SANParks for prioritising human safety despite significant operational challenges, including road and gate closures, power outages and interruptions to basic services.

nnnn

He also announced that SANParks has committed to establishing a Kruger Relief Fund to support rebuilding efforts, emergency supplies and other urgent needs. The fund will be managed and audited by two independent auditing firms to ensure transparency.

nnnn

Although disruptive rainfall may continue in the coming days, the Minister said SANParks and emergency services remain well equipped to manage the situation. Day visits to the Kruger National Park remain prohibited until further notice, while access at several gates is restricted.

nnnn

Entry into the park is currently limited to essential delivery vehicles, airport transfers with valid flight tickets, officials, and guests with confirmed accommodation bookings at Berg-en-Dal, Skukuza and Pretoriuskop camps.

nnnn

Minister Aucamp confirmed that the situation is being closely monitored and that updates will be shared as conditions change. “The safety of guests, staff and infrastructure remains the highest priority,” he said, urging the public to rely on SANParks’ official communication platforms for verified information.

nnnn

“We are grateful that no loss of life has been recorded and that evacuations have been conducted smoothly,” the Minister added, thanking park management and emergency services for their swift response.

nnnn

SANParks is expected to release further details on the Kruger Relief Fund in due course.

post_title: Gogo Nonyane ya Metsi – Weekly Message (19–26 January)
post_content:

Before the stars speak, Gogo first greets the water.

nnnn

This week, the water is quiet but alert. It does not rush, yet it remembers everything. When Gogo Nonyane ya Metsi looks into it, she sees constellations leaning closer to the earth, their light stretching across the surface like threads connecting the heavens to human lives. These are not loud signs. They are whispers from the ancestors, carried by reflection and shadow.

nnnn

The water reveals that many are standing at a crossing: between holding on and letting go, between speaking and remaining silent, between action and patience.

nnnn

Gogo says: “When the stars bend toward the water, they ask us to look inward. What you disturb now will ripple far. What you heal now will settle many seasons.”

nnnn

This is a week for measured steps, honest reflection, and listening more than speaking. The constellations do not demand speed — they ask for awareness. Watch the signs that repeat themselves. Pay attention to dreams, to sudden memories, to words that arrive more than once. These are messages surfacing.

nnnn

Below, each sign receives its message as seen in the water and guided by its constellation for the week of 19–26 January.

nnnn

nnnn

Aries (21 March – 19 April)

nnnnnnnn

Taurus (20 April – 20 May)

nnnnnnnn

Rest near the end of the week restores your strength.

Gemini (21 May – 20 June)

nnnnnnnn

nnnnnnnn

nnnnnnnn

Gogo sees Leo shining proudly among the stars, yet its reflection bends in the water. This is a lesson in humility. Recognition comes, but only if shared. nnnnnnnn

The waters show Virgo’s careful constellation, each star in its place. This is a week of correction and healing. Gogo sees you restoring order — in health, work, or daily routine. Be careful not to fix what does not ask for fixing, especially in relationships. Simplicity brings peace.

nnnnnnnn

Aquarius (20 January – 18 February)

Pisces (19 February – 20 March)

post_title: KNP Introduces Gate Quotas Due to Flood Damage

Visitors have been urged to ensure that their vehicles have sufficient fuel, as filling stations at camps may be affected by the ongoing adverse weather conditions.

Park authorities confirmed that essential delivery vehicles, airport transfers—provided proof of a valid flight ticket is presented—and official vehicles will be permitted entry only through Paul Kruger Gate.

post_title: National Disaster Declared After Severe Floods
post_content:
n

The government has officially declared a national disaster in response to catastrophic severe weather and flooding that have affected several provinces since late December 2025.

nnnn

The classification was confirmed in a statement issued by National Disaster Management Centre, with its head, Elias Sithole, citing the scale and severity of the destruction as the basis for the decision.

nnnn

The declaration follows weeks of torrential rain, lightning and damaging winds that have ravaged Limpopo, Mpumalanga, KwaZulu-Natal, Eastern Cape and the North West.

nnnn

In the official directive, Sithole said the widespread impact of the severe weather left the authorities with no option but to escalate the response.

nnnn

“I regard this occurrence as a disaster and, in terms of Section 23(1)(b) of the Disaster Management Act, 2002, I classify the disaster as a national disaster,” he stated.

nnnn

He noted that the prolonged severe weather has resulted in the loss of life, extensive damage to homes, public infrastructure and the environment, as well as major disruptions to basic services such as electricity, water supply and access to healthcare and education.

nnnn

With the declaration now in place, the primary responsibility for coordinating and managing the disaster response shifts to the National Executive. This enables the mobilisation of additional resources and allows for a more coordinated response across national, provincial and local spheres of government.

nnnn

Sithole has called on all organs of state to strengthen their support to disaster management structures and to ensure that contingency and emergency plans are fully activated to address the ongoing effects of flooding.

nnnn

The National Disaster Management Centre will oversee a multi-sectoral relief and rehabilitation programme aimed at supporting affected communities, restoring essential services and beginning the long process of rebuilding damaged infrastructure across the impacted provinces.

post_title: ActionSA Warns Floods Endanger Mpumalanga Learners
post_content:
n

ActionSA has raised serious concerns over the impact of recent heavy rains and flooding across Mpumalanga, warning that failing infrastructure is placing lives at risk, particularly those of school learners.

nnnn

In a statement issued on Sunday, ActionSA said the provincial government has confirmed that an estimated R2.1 billion is needed to repair flood-damaged infrastructure, including roads and crossings that are critical for mobility, safety and economic activity.

nnnn

The party said the human cost of the floods is even more alarming. The death toll linked to the heavy rains in Mpumalanga has risen sharply, with dozens of lives lost across the province and neighbouring areas.

nnnn

“These are not merely statistics. They are families torn apart and communities traumatised by a tragedy that demands urgent and decisive leadership,” said Thoko Mashiane, an ActionSA Member of the Mpumalanga Legislature.

nnnn

Mashiane highlighted conditions in Matsulu, where learners are reportedly being forced to cross roads that have turned into flowing streams just to get to and from school.

nnnn

“This is extremely dangerous and entirely unacceptable. No child should have to risk their life in order to access an education,” she said.

nnnn

According to ActionSA, the crisis exposes a deeper structural problem in the province, with infrastructure that is not designed to withstand extreme weather events. In many rural areas, communities rely on low-lying crossings that were never properly engineered to endure heavy rainfall.

nnnn

“These structures did not fail by chance. They were inadequate by design,” Mashiane said, adding that the predictable result is flooded roads, isolated communities and lives placed in danger.

nnnn

The party said the R2.1 billion repair bill is evidence of a reactive approach by government, arguing that proper planning, engineering and maintenance could have significantly reduced both the financial burden and the loss of life.

nnnn

ActionSA has called on provincial and national authorities to urgently mobilise additional aid for affected communities, prioritise the restoration of safe access routes—especially those used by learners—and commit to a long-term infrastructure strategy that accounts for climate change and extreme weather.

nnnn

“The people of Mpumalanga deserve infrastructure that protects them, not systems that fail them when they are most vulnerable,” Mashiane said.

post_title: Floods Leave Death, Destruction Across Province
post_content:
n

kAt least 20 people have lost their lives following severe flooding that has devastated large parts of Mpumalanga, leaving thousands of residents displaced and without basic necessities.

nnnn

Provincial authorities estimate that more than 1,500 homes have been damaged or destroyed, forcing families into temporary shelters or leaving them destitute. Critical infrastructure has also taken a heavy knock, with several roads and bridges washed away or rendered unsafe. Preliminary assessments place the cost of the damage at approximately R2 billion.

nnnn

Mpumalanga Premier Mandla Ndlovu has urged residents to remain vigilant and to avoid affected areas, particularly rivers and low-lying zones where water levels remain dangerously high.

nnnn

“One is one too many, so that is why we are making this call to the people of the province to avoid finding themselves in dangerous places, especially our rivers, which are flowing fast,” Ndlovu said.

nnnn

The floods follow days of relentless rainfall linked to severe weather systems affecting several parts of the country. Emergency services, disaster management teams and volunteers have been deployed to assist affected communities, conduct search-and-rescue operations and provide humanitarian relief.

nnnn

President Cyril Ramaphosa has pledged national government support to assist Mpumalanga as it recovers from the disaster. On Monday, Ramaphosa visited the province to conduct oversight inspections in some of the worst-hit areas.

nnnnnnnn

The President confirmed that government would adopt an “all-hands-on-deck” approach in response to weather-related disasters impacting Mpumalanga, as well as Limpopo and KwaZulu-Natal.

nnnn

Engagements are already under way with the National Treasury following the official disaster classification of the affected regions. Ramaphosa said the scale of the damage requires urgent and coordinated intervention from all spheres of government.

nnnn

“Our Minister of Finance is in Davos, but we are briefing him, and we’re going to see what intervention the government is able to make,” the President said.

nnnn

While acknowledging the swift response by emergency and disaster management teams, Ramaphosa stressed that more resources and long-term solutions are needed.

nnnn

“As government response has been effective, obviously, we need to do more to deal with disasters that continue to befall us,” he said.

nnnn

Authorities have warned that further rainfall could worsen conditions, and residents are encouraged to heed official alerts, cooperate with emergency services and prioritise safety as recovery efforts continue

post_title: SACC urges united faith response to devastating floods
post_content:
n

The South African Council of Churches (SACC) has called for a united response from faith communities following severe flooding that has affected large parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga.

nnnn

In a media statement issued on Tuesday, SACC General Secretary Rev Mzwandile Molo expressed solidarity with communities impacted by persistent heavy rainfall over recent days. The flooding has caused widespread damage to homes, roads and bridges, disrupted essential services and claimed lives. Government has since classified the situation as a National Disaster to strengthen coordination and accelerate relief efforts.

nnnn

The SACC said it was deeply moved by reports of up to 30 people having lost their lives, with others still missing. Rev Molo conveyed heartfelt condolences to bereaved families and assured prayers for those whose loved ones remain unaccounted for.

nnnn

Quoting Galatians 6:2, “Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfil the law of Christ,” the council emphasised the importance of compassion and shared responsibility during the crisis. Prayers were also extended to families who have been displaced or traumatised by the floods.

nnnn

The statement raised serious concern about the risks posed by damaged infrastructure, including washed-away bridges, submerged roads and overflowing rivers. These conditions have left some communities isolated from clinics, schools, food supply routes and emergency services. Residents were urged to prioritise safety and strictly heed official warnings, particularly by avoiding flooded roads and fast-moving streams.

nnnn

While welcoming the declaration of a National Disaster, the SACC stressed that disaster funding and procurement processes must be handled honestly and transparently. Rev Molo warned that such emergencies should never be exploited for corruption or the abuse of public resources.

nnnn

The council also acknowledged and gave thanks for the relief efforts already underway, particularly those led by faith-based institutions, including SACC member churches, which have been providing support to affected families and vulnerable groups.

nnnn

In addition, the SACC affirmed its support for a coordinated response involving the South African Women in Dialogue (SAWID), partnering non-governmental organisations, independent human rights defenders and private sector collaborators. Churches and faith groups were encouraged to continue supporting these initiatives.

nnnn

Clergy and people of faith were further urged to offer pastoral care rooted in compassion, especially to families facing loss, displacement and fear.

nnnn

The SACC concluded by praying that God’s mercy and grace would continue to sustain the people of Limpopo and Mpumalanga during this difficult period.

post_title: Learner Fatally Stabbed at School
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Department of Education has expressed shock and deep sadness following the tragic death of a 19-year-old Grade 11 learner at LD Moetanalo Secondary School in the Steve Tshwete Circuit 1, within the Steve Tshwete Local Municipality.

nnnn

The incident occurred on Tuesday, 20 January 2026, while learners were changing classes on the school premises. School management acted promptly by informing the learner’s parents and reporting the matter to the South African Police Service. Police investigations are currently under way, and a fellow learner is alleged to be involved in the incident. The suspect reportedly fled the scene and is being sought by authorities.

The Department of Education has strongly condemned the incident, emphasising that violence in schools poses a serious threat to the safety and wellbeing of learners, educators and support staff. Such acts also undermine the constitutional right to education and the creation of safe learning environments.

In response to the tragedy, the MEC for Education in Mpumalanga, Ms Lindi Masina, is expected to visit the school and the bereaved family on Wednesday, 21 January 2026. The visit aims to convey condolences, assess the situation on the ground and receive a detailed report on the incident.

Officials from the Department’s Inclusive Education and Wellness Unit have also been deployed to provide psychosocial support to learners, educators and staff affected by the incident.

nnnn

The Department has extended its heartfelt condolences to the family, friends and the entire LD Moetanalo Secondary School community during this painful time.

nnnn

May the learner’s soul rest in peace.

post_title: MEGA Responds to Floods Affecting Mpumalanga Economy
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Economic Growth Agency (MEGA) has expressed deep concern for residents, families, and businesses affected by the recent severe floods across the province.

The extreme weather has damaged key infrastructure, including roads, bridges, and transport routes, disrupting trade and supply chains for agriculture, retail, and industry. Hundreds of kilometres of road networks are affected, temporarily blocking access to important markets and slowing economic activity. Homes, businesses, and public facilities have also suffered significant damage.

MEGA CEO Isaac Mahlangu said the agency is committed to supporting recovery efforts, including restoring infrastructure, market access, and affected enterprises. He emphasised collaboration with government, private sector partners, and communities to minimise long-term economic impacts.

MEGA acknowledged President Cyril Ramaphosa’s visit to Nkomazi, highlighting national support for recovery, and praised disaster management teams and volunteers for their tireless efforts.
