post_title: Floods Leave Scars, Hope Emerges
post_content:
n

Heavy rains have left a trail of grief and destruction across Mpumalanga and Limpopo, turning once-familiar villages into scenes of loss, uncertainty and resilience. In Bushbuckridge and neighbouring areas, families are still counting the cost as floodwaters recede, revealing damaged homes, shattered belongings and lives forever changed.

nnnn

According to an update delivered this week by Minister of Human Settlements, Thembi Simelane, the human toll continues to rise. Limpopo has now recorded 18 fatalities, with six people still missing across Limpopo and Mpumalanga. In Mpumalanga alone, 20 lives have been lost. Behind each number is a story of a family waiting for answers, a community mourning one of its own.

nnnn

The physical damage is just as stark. In Limpopo, 1 942 houses have been damaged, while Mpumalanga has recorded 1 808 affected homes. Many of these are mud structures in rural villages, which stood little chance against relentless rains. For families who had already been living on the margins, the floods have deepened hardship and exposed long-standing vulnerabilities.

nnnn

Government teams are now racing against time and weather conditions to bring relief. Verification processes are under way to assess the extent of damage and determine appropriate assistance. Despite difficult conditions, the Department of Human Settlements has begun moving ahead with support for households already verified.

nnnn

Temporary Emergency Accommodation is being procured for families currently housed in evacuation and mass care centres. In a move that brings some relief closer to home, 73 Temporary Residential Units have been earmarked for Bushbuckridge, with additional units planned for Mbaula, Blouberg and Makhado. These structures are expected to offer affected families a measure of safety and dignity while longer-term solutions are developed.

nnnn

Over the coming days, national and provincial leaders will be on the ground in both provinces, working alongside local authorities to ensure aid reaches those who need it most. Yet, amid the devastation, there have been powerful moments of solidarity. Churches, community groups and NGOs have opened their doors, shared food, offered shelter and reminded many that they are not alone.

nnnn

As floodwaters fade from the roads and fields, the real work begins: rebuilding homes, restoring hope and ensuring communities are better protected against future disasters. For Bushbuckridge and many other towns, recovery will take time, but resilience, compassion and collective effort are already lighting the way forward.

n

post_title: Life Terms for Quadruple Murder
post_content:
n

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the South African Police Service (SAPS) in Mpumalanga has welcomed the sentencing of a 57-year-old man convicted on four counts of murder.

nnnn

Africa Thembinkosi Shongwe was sentenced by the Breyten High Court sitting in Mbombela on Thursday, 22 January 2026, following a thorough investigation into the deaths of an adult woman and her three minor children.

nnnn

The court heard that on 25 February 2023, neighbours at Phola Park became concerned when a woman, known for escorting her children to and from school daily, was not seen that morning. After checking on her home, neighbours noticed worrying signs and immediately alerted the police.

nnnn

Upon entering the house, SAPS members discovered four deceased persons in two rooms. The victims were identified as the woman and her three children, including twin boys and a girl.

nnnn

A comprehensive investigation led to the arrest of Shongwe, a citizen of the Kingdom of Eswatini and the biological father of one of the children. He was charged with four counts of murder, as well as contravening South Africa’s Immigration Act for being in the country without valid documentation.

nnnn

Shongwe pleaded guilty to all charges on 19 January 2026. On sentencing, the court imposed life imprisonment on each of the four murder counts and declared him unfit to possess a firearm.

nnnn

Welcoming the outcome, Acting Provincial Commissioner Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi praised the cooperation between investigators, prosecutors and the judiciary. He also commended community members for their vigilance and swift action in reporting the matter to authorities.

nnnn

SAPS reiterated its commitment to protecting communities and ensuring that serious crimes are thoroughly investigated and successfully prosecuted.

post_title: Kruger Flood Recovery Fund Launched
post_content:
n

The Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, Willie Aucamp, has provided a comprehensive update on the impact of recent floods on the Kruger National Park and surrounding provinces, while announcing the establishment of the SANParks Kruger Recovery Fund to support long-term restoration efforts.

nnnn

Speaking on Thursday, 22 January 2026, the Minister said his recent visit to the flood-stricken park left a lasting impression on him, describing the scale of destruction as devastating. The severe weather has affected not only the Kruger National Park but large parts of Mpumalanga and Limpopo, where lives have been lost and homes and critical infrastructure damaged. He reaffirmed that the declaration of a National Disaster in terms of the Disaster Management Act of 2002 was both necessary and appropriate.

nnnn

In the Kruger National Park alone, damage to infrastructure is estimated to run into hundreds of millions of rand. Roads, bridges, water systems and electricity services have been severely affected, while staff villages and tourist accommodation have also suffered extensive damage. Despite the scale of destruction, the Minister highlighted that no lives were lost inside the park, crediting SANParks’ early warning systems and the swift response of park management and emergency services for the safe evacuation of all staff and visitors.

nnnnnnnn

The floods have had a significant impact on tourism operations. Fifteen camps remain closed, some of them completely inaccessible due to washed-away roads and bridges. Temporary gate closures are still in place in certain areas, limiting both day and overnight visits. Between 9 and 19 January 2026, the park recorded 24,073 guest entries, a decline of 41 per cent compared to the same period last year. The Minister warned that this will result in immediate to medium-term revenue losses, placing pressure on SANParks, which generates nearly 80 per cent of its operating budget through tourism.

nnnn

The latest floods have compounded challenges from previous flooding in 2023, from which the park was still recovering. According to the Minister, the combined impact has exceeded existing contingency and maintenance budgets, increasing the risk of prolonged recovery delays, environmental degradation and socio-economic consequences for surrounding communities.

nnnn

To address these challenges, the Minister confirmed the establishment of the SANParks Kruger Recovery Fund, which he said is essential to ensuring the long-term sustainability of the park as a national heritage asset and economic driver. The fund will be administered with strict fiduciary oversight through three independent audit firms on SANParks’ panel, providing transparency and accountability to donors.

nnnn

Support for the fund has already been received from across society, including pensioners, young people, and both local and international organisations. The SANParks Honorary Rangers will play a key role through their “Kruger Flood 2026 Fund” fundraising campaign, while internationally acclaimed author Tony Park has also committed to supporting the recovery efforts.

nnnn

The Minister cautioned the public that the SANParks Kruger Recovery Fund and the Honorary Rangers’ Kruger Flood 2026 Fund are the only legitimate channels authorised to receive donations, warning against the risk of fraudulent fundraising during times of crisis.

nnnn

Providing an update on conditions in the park, the Minister said several roads in both the northern and southern regions remain inaccessible, with multiple rest camps closed due to flood damage. While Malelane, Numbi and Paul Kruger gates remain open, access is controlled through an entry quota system, and the northern and southern regions of the park are still cut off from each other.

nnnn

Concluding his address, the Minister called on South Africans and the international community to support the recovery of the Kruger National Park. He emphasised that the park is not only a conservation area but an economic lifeline for the region and a symbol of South Africa’s natural heritage. As the park marks its centenary this year, he said collective action is vital to ensure it remains protected for future generations.

post_title: Man Killed in Calcutta Shooting

nnnn

According to the South African Police Service (SAPS), officers were conducting routine patrols in the Mkhuhlu area at about 7.30pm when they received information about a shooting. Police immediately proceeded to the scene, where they discovered a white Isuzu bakkie with Mpumalanga registration plates riddled with bullet holes. The rear window of the vehicle had also been damaged.

nnnn

Inside the bakkie, police found the lifeless body of a 56-year-old man. Preliminary investigations revealed that the victim had just left his home and was attacked a few metres from his residence. Spent cartridges from a high-calibre firearm were also recovered at the scene.

nnnn

The motive for the killing is still unknown and forms part of the ongoing investigation. No arrests have been made at this stage.

nnnn

post_title: Healing Where Tradition Meets Medicine
post_content:
n

In Bushbuckridge, where ancestral knowledge remains a trusted source of care alongside clinics and hospitals, Lesaka La Dingaka is helping to bring two worlds of healing closer together.

nnnn

Founded in 2007 as a non-profit organisation, Lesaka La Dingaka promotes cooperation between Traditional Health Practitioners (THPs), faith-based healers and Western medical practitioners, working to ensure rural communities are not excluded from safe, coordinated healthcare.

nnnn

For many families in villages across Bushbuckridge, traditional healers are still the first point of contact during illness, distress or uncertainty. Lesaka La Dingaka was established to organise, educate and help regulate THPs, while building stronger working relationships with clinics, hospitals and key government partners, particularly the Department of Health.

nnnn

Leadership rooted in calling and community

nnnn

At local level, the organisation is coordinated by Dr MN Mnisi, the Mpumalanga Coordinator of Lesaka La Dingaka and a respected traditional health practitioner from Xanthia Village. He was initiated in 2010 at Cork Trust under Gobela Mpandezithi Mavis Mhangane, and is known for his commitment to both cultural responsibility and public health realities.

nnnn

At national level, Lesaka La Dingaka is led by Director Elizabeth Baas, initiated in 1989 by veteran traditional healer Nyoniyezwe Mkhabela. Mkhabela, born 16 April 1918, was initiated in 1974 and is still actively practising and training amathwasa, continuing to shape the generations that carry traditional healing forward.

nnnn

Building safe referral pathways

nnnn

A key focus of the organisation is education and patient safety. Lesaka La Dingaka trains THPs to recognise conditions that require urgent medical attention, and to confidently refer patients to clinics and hospitals when needed. This helps reduce delays in treatment and builds trust between communities and formal healthcare services.

nnnn

The organisation also raises awareness about the dangers of toxic and unregulated medicines, promoting responsible practices that protect lives.

nnnn

Care that goes beyond medicine

nnnn

Lesaka La Dingaka’s work extends into psycho-social support, connecting individuals and families to professional services when dealing with trauma, mental health concerns or social distress.

nnnn

It also supports vulnerable households through practical interventions, including meals for orphaned and vulnerable children and assistance to destitute community members. Through home visits, the organisation reaches the elderly, the ill and those who struggle to access formal services — offering dignity, guidance and human connection.

nnnn

Prevention, awareness and community education

nnnn

Lesaka La Dingaka promotes a drug-free environment and speaks out against substance abuse through community dialogues and education. It also addresses HIV and AIDS, TB, STIs, cancer and mental health in culturally sensitive ways that encourage early intervention and reduce stigma.

nnnn

Strengthening unity among healers

nnnn

To improve coordination and accountability, the organisation is developing a database of Traditional Health Practitioners and hosting regular engagements where healers can share knowledge, align practices and strengthen cooperation with clinics and hospitals.

nnnn

A local symbol of unity

nnnn

In Bushbuckridge and across Mpumalanga, Lesaka La Dingaka continues to show that true wellness is strongest when tradition and modern medicine work side by side — placing the wellbeing of communities at the centre of every decision.

ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa has told the party’s top leadership that the organisation must shift “decisively from talk to implementation”, warning that South Africans want visible change, not speeches and slogans.

He said the party must focus on practical changes that improve people’s lives — from how government programmes are implemented to how officials are held accountable for results.

The ANC’s public communications around the lekgotla stressed execution and accountability, with commission work intended to consolidate policy direction and implementation plans.

post_title: Department Denies E-Learning Procurement Claims
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Department of Education has strongly refuted allegations of wastage and irregular procurement relating to its e-learning devices programme, following reports published by City Press and News24.

nnnn

In a statement issued on 26 January 2026, the Department said the claims misrepresent the facts surrounding the Ubuhlebuzile E-Learning Programme, which was introduced in 2022 as a phased and strategic intervention to improve teaching and learning across the province.

nnnn

According to the Department, 64 000 tablets were procured in 2022 for Grade 12 learners under a three-year SITA-facilitated contract valued at R224 million, which included a three-year warranty. Bongani Rainmaker Limited (BRL) was appointed as the supplier in full compliance with government procurement regulations.

nnnn

In 2025, these devices were replaced with 60 000 Packard Bell tablets at a cost of R232 million, also inclusive of a three-year warranty. The Department confirmed that the tablets were successfully distributed to Grade 12 learners in quintile 1 to 3 schools and stated that it has received no verified reports of widespread device failure.

nnnn

The Department further attributed the improvement in Grade 12 results — from 79% in 2023 to 86.55% in 2025 — partly to the effective use of e-learning tools introduced through the programme.

nnnn

It rejected claims that the Packard Bell tablets constituted wastage, explaining that the devices issued to the 2025 Grade 12 cohort have been retrieved, reformatted and reloaded with updated content. They will be re-issued to the 2026 Grade 12 learners as part of a cost-efficient and sustainable approach.

nnnn

Looking ahead, the Department confirmed that it has placed an order for 70 000 Windows-based tablet notebooks for Grade 10 learners in 2026, at a cost of R330 million — not R600 million as alleged. These devices will be retained by learners from Grade 10 through to Grade 12, with content updated remotely to reduce future logistics and redistribution costs.

nnnn

The procurement process, facilitated through BRL, allows the service provider to source Department-approved devices, load educational content and manage distribution. Funding is drawn from a dedicated e-learning budget, supplemented by the Learning and Teaching Support Material (LTSM) allocation.

nnnn

For the 2025/26 financial year, the Department allocated R717 million to the e-learning programme, covering both Grade 10 and Grade 12 learners.

nnnn

The Department reiterated that all procurement processes were lawful, strategic and focused on improving learner outcomes, adding that allegations of inflated costs, wastage or non-functional devices are misleading and incorrect.

nnnn

It reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, accountability and the effective use of technology to advance quality education throughout Mpumalanga.

post_title: Bheki Nyathikazi: Voice for public service
post_content:
n

In Mpumalanga’s noisy information space, where rumours travel faster than facts and headlines often outrun context, Bheki Nyathikazi represents a quieter but essential craft: the discipline of communication as public service.

nnnn

Nyathikazi serves as Media Liaison Officer in the Communication Services unit within Mpumalanga’s Department of Agriculture, Rural Development, Land and Environmental Affairs (DARDLEA). That job title sounds administrative until you consider what it demands in practice: translating government processes into language communities can trust, correcting misinformation without inflaming tensions, and ensuring that public programmes do not remain invisible simply because they were poorly explained.

nnnn

What makes Nyathikazi notable is that he is not “just” a spokesperson. He is also a communications practitioner and former journalist, writing publicly in his personal capacity. That background matters. It suggests an understanding of how newsrooms work, how audiences receive information, and how quickly credibility can be lost when communication becomes defensive, vague, or overly polished.

nnnn

His writing and public commentary reflect a preoccupation with standards: what journalism should be, what public debate should look like, and what community life can become when neglect is normalised. On Mail & Guardian’s platform, he has tackled issues as practical as the condition of taxi ranks and as principled as interview ethics and fairness in the media. These are not “safe” topics; they are the kinds of conversations that force institutions, professionals and the public to look in the mirror.

nnnn

In a recent online exchange about the pressures facing newsrooms, Nyathikazi argued for deeper, more human storytelling—work that does not simply chase what is already trending. For community journalism in places like Bushbuckridge, that idea lands with weight. Our strongest stories are rarely the loudest. They are the ones that explain the “why”, elevate ordinary people, and hold power to account without reducing communities to crises.

nnnn

The challenge, of course, is that communication in government is only valuable when it is timely, transparent and measurable. A media liaison officer can open doors, but departments must keep those doors open with consistent information, accessible channels, and respect for the public’s right to know.

nnnn

Nyathikazi’s career arc—journalism into public-sector communications—suggests a belief that words can still improve the lived reality of communities. In a province that often battles with service-delivery frustrations and distrust, that belief is not sentimental. It is strategic.

post_title: Stricter Online Safety Measures for Children
post_content:
n

South Africa is considering tougher measures to safeguard children online, including the criminalisation of exposing minors to pornographic material.

nnnn

The proposals form part of the Draft White Paper on Audio and Audiovisual Media Services and Online Safety, currently under consideration by the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies. Departmental spokesperson Tlangelani Manganyi said the measures are aimed at strengthening protections for children in an increasingly digital world.

nnnn

According to Manganyi, the proposed interventions seek to shield children from harmful content that could negatively affect their physical, mental or moral development. “The intention is to ensure that children are not exposed to disturbing and harmful material, or prematurely introduced to adult experiences,” he said.

nnnn

The move comes amid a global push for stricter online safety regulations for children. Australia recently introduced the world’s first ban on social media use for children under the age of 16. In Europe, France has passed legislation restricting access to certain websites for children under 15.

nnnn

Social media platforms are also facing mounting pressure from regulators. TikTok has announced that it will begin rolling out new age-detection technology across Europe as part of efforts to identify and remove users under the age of 13. Meanwhile, the European Parliament is advocating for mandatory age limits on social media platforms, and Denmark has proposed a ban on social media use for children under 15.

nnnn

In the United Kingdom, a pilot programme aimed at enforcing age restrictions has already resulted in the removal of thousands of users found to be under the age of 13.

nnnn

Manganyi emphasised that South Africa’s approach would build on the existing mandate of the Film and Publication Board (FPB). “The FPB currently regulates the creation, production, possession and distribution of films, games and certain publications to provide consumer advice that enables people to make informed viewing, reading and gaming choices for themselves and for children in their care,” he said.

nnnn

The proposed changes signal a stronger stance by government to adapt legislation to the realities of digital media and online platforms, while placing the protection and wellbeing of children at the centre of policy development.

nnnn

Public consultations on the Draft White Paper are expected to guide the final shape of the proposed regulations.

nnnn

post_title: Reserve Bank Holds Interest Rates Steady at 6.75%
post_content:
n

The South African Reserve Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has decided to keep the repo rate unchanged at 6.75%, meaning the prime lending rate remains at 10.25%.

nnnn

The decision was taken during this week’s MPC meeting, where four members voted to hold the rate steady, while two supported a 25-basis-point cut. The outcome comes after annual headline consumer inflation edged slightly higher to 3.6% in December.

nnnn

Reserve Bank Governor Lesetja Kganyago described 2025 as a “watershed year” for South Africa’s economy, despite ongoing global uncertainty.

nnnn

“Despite a volatile global backdrop, there was significant progress on domestic reforms, including a new inflation target,” Kganyago said. “These efforts have been rewarded with lower borrowing costs, a rapid decline in inflation expectations, and steadier growth.”

nnnn

For households and businesses carrying debt, the decision brings some relief, as monthly loan repayments will not increase. However, some economists believe there was room for a small interest rate cut to further support economic growth.

nnnn

Kganyago said the MPC remains focused on stabilising inflation at 3% over the next few years. He cautioned that in a less favourable scenario, inflation could peak at around 4%, with a slower return to the target.

nnnn

“In such a case, interest rates would remain largely unchanged in the near term, with the move towards a neutral level delayed by about a year,” he said.

nnnn

For local communities, the steady interest rate offers short-term certainty, while the broader focus remains on controlling inflation and supporting sustainable economic growth.

post_title: South Africa’s prisons under strain from overcrowding
post_content:
n

South Africa’s correctional facilities continue to face severe overcrowding, with more than 170,000 inmates detained nationwide during the recent festive season, far exceeding the system’s approved capacity.

nnnn

The Department of Correctional Services (DCS) has confirmed that prisons across the country are designed to accommodate just over 107,000 inmates. This means tens of thousands of offenders are being housed in facilities already stretched beyond their intended limits, placing immense pressure on infrastructure and staff.

nnnn

Addressing a media briefing on Monday, Correctional Services Commissioner Samuel Thobakgale said the current situation represents the highest prison population recorded in recent years.

nnnn

“This level of incarceration has placed immense pressure on infrastructure, staffing, security management and the department’s budget,” Thobakgale said. He added that the strain was worsened by reduced court activity during the festive season, which slows down the movement of cases and the release of eligible offenders.

nnnn

nnnn

For many households, the biggest immediate benefit may be in transport and essential goods. post_title: Mozambican National Jailed for Drug Trafficking

n

A 39-year-old Mozambican national has been sentenced to ten years’ imprisonment for drug trafficking following his arrest at the Lebombo Port of Entry in Mpumalanga.

nnnn

According to the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (the Hawks), the operation unfolded in June 2024 when members of the South African Police Service intercepted a minibus entering South Africa from Mozambique. The vehicle was found to be carrying 17 containers of crystal methamphetamine weighing a total of 17 kilograms, with an estimated street value of R4.25 million.

nnnn

The accused, Jorge Salomao Chimene, was the sole occupant of the minibus. The drugs were concealed in various compartments of the vehicle, including inside speakers, indicating an intention to smuggle the narcotics into the country.

nnnn

Following his arrest, the case was handed over to the Hawks’ Serious Organised Crime Investigation unit based in Nelspruit. Investigators successfully opposed bail after presenting evidence that the drugs were destined for distribution within South Africa.

nnnn

Chimene appeared in court on Thursday, 29 January 2026, where he pleaded guilty to possession of drugs. He was sentenced to ten years’ imprisonment, with seven years suspended for three years on condition that he is not convicted of a similar offence during that period. This means he will serve an effective three years behind bars.

nnnn

The Provincial Head of the Hawks in Mpumalanga, Major General Nico Gerber, welcomed the sentence, saying it sent a strong message to those involved in drug trafficking. He described the distribution of drugs as a serious crime that destroys lives and communities.

nnnn

Police have reiterated their commitment to combating cross-border drug trafficking and protecting communities from the harmful effects of illegal substances.

post_title: Parliament’s Ad Hoc Committee Moves on Ramaphosa
post_content:
n

Cape Town — South Africa’s Parliament is preparing to send written questions to President Cyril Ramaphosa amid ongoing controversy over allegations of political interference in the criminal justice system. The Ad Hoc Committee investigating testimony about the disbanded Political Killings Task Team (PKTT) agreed to commission its legal advisers to draft a set of questions for the President. 

nnnn

The decision follows a tense virtual meeting on Monday, during which committee members debated whether Mr Ramaphosa should be summoned to testify in person. Several witnesses during earlier hearings referenced the President in connection with decisions taken over the PKTT, which was established to investigate assassinations of political figures and community leaders in KwaZulu-Natal. 

nnnn

EFF leader Julius Malema, who sits on the committee, argued that Mr Ramaphosa should face the same scrutiny as any other witness. “Anything else that Madlanga was subjected to, the President can be subjected to,” Mr Malema said, emphasising that parliamentary processes, not party hierarchies, should determine proceedings. 

nnnn

Soviet Lekganyane, the committee chairperson, stressed that due process would guide the committee’s next steps. Members will have an opportunity to contribute to the list of written questions, and any further action — including whether the President might be asked to appear in person — will depend on the responses received. 

nnnn

The PKTT’s disbandment on 31 December 2024 has sparked deep controversy. Suspended Police Minister Senzo Mchunu testified that he briefed President Ramaphosa on the decision and that the President agreed with it, a claim that has fuelled calls for further clarification. Other witnesses, including KwaZulu-Natal Police Commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi, suggested that Mr Ramaphosa may not have been fully informed before the task team was dissolved. 

nnnn

Other testimony has highlighted contradictions within the South African Police Service (SAPS) about whether the PKTT was formally disbanded at all, and concerns have been raised about delays in investigations into politically linked killings. 

nnnn

The committee’s work is part of a broader inquiry into allegations of corruption and political interference in law enforcement agencies. It has already questioned senior figures including Mr Mchunu and the head of the National Prosecuting Authority, Advocate Shamila Batohi, as part of a series of hearings that aim to restore public confidence in the justice system. 

nnnn

As the draft questions are finalised and sent to the Presidency, national attention will remain on how executive accountability and parliamentary oversight interact in one of South Africa’s most sensitive political investigations in recent years.

post_content:

Visitors to Kruger National Park are beginning to see improved access after the severe January 2026 floods, which damaged roads, bridges, tourism facilities and staff accommodation across the park.

nnnn

The park’s H7 Route between Orpen Gate and Satara Rest Camp has now reopened to traffic. Heavy vehicles exceeding eight tonnes are not permitted through the affected section.

nnnn

To maintain movement while repairs and reconstruction continue, the parks authority said it is building a bypass using the S12 and S40 routes. This alternative route is expected to support accessibility during ongoing work at the dam area.

Several visitor sites have also reopened as of Monday. These include Tsendze Rustic Camp near Mopani Rest Camp, the Masorini Ruins near Phalaborwa Gate, as well as the Mooiplaas Picnic Site and Babalala Picnic Site picnic sites.

post_title: Operation Shanela II Nets Hundreds
post_content:
n

Operation Shanela II has delivered significant law-enforcement gains across Mpumalanga, with hundreds of arrests and major confiscations recorded between 29 January and 1 February 2026.

nnnn

The multi-agency operation, coordinated by the South African Police Service (SAPS), brought together Traffic Police, law-enforcement agencies, the South African National Defence Force, the Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, private security and Community Policing Forums.

nnnn

During the operation, officers searched 399 premises, stopped and searched more than 3,000 people and over 1,200 vehicles, and conducted extensive patrols, roadblocks and checkpoints across the province. Detectives also traced 11 wanted suspects, while specialised teams carried out tracking operations and hostel searches.

nnnn

Compliance inspections formed a key part of the operation. Police closed one unlicensed liquor outlet and inspected more than 220 licensed outlets. Inspections were also carried out at second-hand dealers, scrap yards, firearm-holding institutions, farms, mines and both formal and informal businesses to ensure compliance with labour and safety laws.

nnnn

Arrests were made for a wide range of serious offences, including murder, attempted murder, rape, armed robbery, carjacking, assault and burglary. Police also arrested suspects for drug-related crimes, illegal possession of firearms and ammunition, dealing in illicit liquor, driving under the influence, and immigration offences. In total, more than 100 undocumented immigrants were detained.

nnnn

Large quantities of drugs were seized, including over two tonnes of dagga, along with crack cocaine, crystal meth, nyaope and mandrax. Police also confiscated firearms, ammunition, dangerous weapons, fireworks, illegal cigarettes, contraband goods, copper cables and several vehicles.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, praised the operation’s outcomes, saying the results demonstrated the impact of integrated, intelligence-driven policing.

nnnn

“These outcomes send a strong message that crime will not be tolerated. We remain resolute in our mandate to protect the people of Mpumalanga and uphold the rule of law,” he said.

nnnn

Police have indicated that similar high-impact operations will continue as part of ongoing efforts to improve safety and restore order in communities across the province.

post_title: Families of Lily Mine Victims Renew Call for Justice
post_content:
n

Ten years after the Lily Mine collapse, the families of Pretty Nkambule, Yvonne Mnisi, and Solomon Nyirenda have lodged a formal complaint with the South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC). nnnn

ActionSA, led by Herman Mashaba, stood with the families on 5 February 2026, marking the tenth anniversary and renewing calls for justice. An inquest found that mine management failed in risk assessments, while authorities failed to curb illegal mining, contributing to the collapse.

nnnn

Mashaba said: “Three people vanished, and if we think it only happened to these families, it could happen to yours tomorrow. Lily Mine must remain top of mind.”

nnnn

The SAHRC is expected to investigate whether the NPA and Department of Mineral Resources have failed in their duties, while the families continue to demand accountability.

The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) has suspended more than 70,000 social grant payments after beneficiaries were found to be non-compliant during a national eligibility review process.

nnnn

The agency confirmed that a total of 240,000 social grant payments were reviewed as part of efforts to ensure that all recipients still qualify for assistance based on their current financial and personal circumstances. The review process was conducted in cooperation with the National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS) and the South African Revenue Service (SARS), allowing for cross-checking of income, student funding and employment data.

nnnn

SASSA leadership briefed the media in Cape Town on Thursday, outlining the agency’s intensified campaign to protect the integrity of the social grant system and prevent fraud.

nnnn

SASSA Chief Executive Officer, Mr Themba Matlou, said the measures introduced were already producing results.

nnnn

“These measures go a long way in detecting and preventing fraud cases in the social grant system. We have also implemented life certification for identified beneficiaries, and the review of targeted beneficiary groups,” said Matlou.

nnnn

He added that for the current financial year, SASSA had planned to conduct 420,000 beneficiary reviews. By the third quarter, just under 400,000 beneficiaries had already been notified to present themselves for verification.

nnnn

As part of its anti-fraud strategy, SASSA last year introduced compulsory biometric enrolment for all new social grant applications. This system is aimed at preventing identity fraud and ensuring that grants are paid only to qualifying individuals.

nnnn

The Department of Social Development previously revealed that in 2024, SASSA had paid approximately R140 million to beneficiaries who were already deceased, highlighting the scale of irregularities within the system.

nnnn

SASSA has urged all beneficiaries who have been notified for review to cooperate fully, warning that failure to comply may result in the suspension or termination of grant payments. The agency says the process is necessary to protect public funds and ensure that social assistance reaches those who genuinely need it most.

nnnn

post_title: Families Must Speak Up On Abuse
post_content:
n

South Africa will not defeat gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF) unless families speak openly with their children and report abuse without fear, Justice and Constitutional Development Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi has warned.

nnnn

Addressing residents at a Community Outreach Imbizo and Pre-State of the Nation Address (SONA) community activation at the Dulcie September Civic Hall in Athlone, Western Cape, Kubayi said incidents of sexual violence must never be hidden or treated as “private” matters.

nnnn

“When something like this happens, we don’t sit on it and hide it. There cannot be a debate when there is rape… it is a crime,” she said.

nnnn

Kubayi stressed that parents have both a legal and moral duty to report child sexual abuse, including teenage pregnancies involving minors. She emphasised that a child cannot legally consent to sex and that pregnancy involving an underage child amounts to statutory rape.

nnnn

“There is no 11-year-old who can give consent to sex. The age of consent is clear in the law. When a child becomes pregnant, it is statutory rape,” she said.

nnnn

The Minister urged families to act immediately by seeking medical care and reporting cases to the police. She added that teachers and community members share the same responsibility to protect children and report abuse.

nnnn

Kubayi also raised concerns about cases where families conceal teenage pregnancies after accepting financial settlements from perpetrators. She warned that such deals protect offenders and expose other children to harm.

nnnn

“You may spend that R50 000 and it will be finished, but you have a child who is destroyed for life. Once you do that, the perpetrator moves from this child to another,” she said.

nnnn

Kubayi said perpetrators must be held accountable regardless of their status in a household, including if they are breadwinners. She added that abuse affects both girls and boys, calling on civil society and community activists to help fight what she described as a growing pandemic.

nnnn

Government, she said, has amended legislation and is considering further reforms, including allowing the publication of convicted offenders’ names to prioritise victims over perpetrators

post_title: Operation Shanela II cracks down on crime
post_content:
n

Operation Shanela II has delivered a major blow against crime in Mpumalanga, following a province-wide law-enforcement operation conducted between 5 and 8 February 2026.

nnnn

The coordinated operation brought together multiple stakeholders, including the South African Police Service (SAPS), Traffic Police, various law-enforcement agencies, the Departments of Home Affairs, Health, Labour and Correctional Services, private security companies, and Community Policing Forums (CPFs).

nnnn

During the operation, law-enforcement teams carried out extensive activities across the province. A total of 275 premises were searched, while 4 285 people and 1 975 vehicles were stopped and searched. Police also conducted 1 106 stop-and-search operations, six specialised tracking operations, and 3 474 high-visibility patrols, which included 109 vehicle checkpoints, 26 roadblocks and 2 262 patrols. Detectives conducted 93 tracing operations for wanted suspects, and six hostels were searched.

nnnn

Significant compliance and inspection operations were also undertaken. Six unlicensed liquor outlets were closed, while 282 licensed liquor outlets were inspected. Police inspected 91 second-hand dealers, issuing two notices for non-compliance, and visited 25 scrap yards and recyclers. Firearm compliance inspections were conducted at both non-official and official institutions, including private security companies and state facilities.

nnnn

Labour-law compliance inspections were carried out at 132 informal businesses, including spaza shops, and 22 formal businesses in the hospitality and retail sectors. Joint operations with the Departments of Home Affairs and Labour saw 78 farms and one mine inspected, while enforcement actions were also conducted in terms of the SASREA and Regulation of Gatherings Act.

nnnn

Numerous arrests were made during the operation, including wanted suspects linked to serious crimes such as murder, rape, carjacking, assault GBH and illegal possession of firearms. Additional arrests were recorded for a wide range of offences, including drug dealing and possession, illegal liquor trading, possession of dangerous weapons, firearm and ammunition offences, serious violent crimes, burglary, driving under the influence, and human trafficking. A total of 70 illegal immigrants were also arrested.

nnnn

Large quantities of illegal items were confiscated, including drugs, firearms, ammunition, dangerous weapons, alcohol, copper cables, cash, contraband goods and vehicles. Drug seizures included dagga, crack cocaine, crystal meth (tik), nyaope, mandrax tablets and mandrax powder.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, praised all law-enforcement agencies and stakeholders for the successful execution of the operation.

nnnn

He said the sustained, integrated approach demonstrated SAPS’ unwavering commitment to decisively combat crime and restore safety and order across Mpumalanga.

nnnn

Operation Shanela II is expected to continue strengthening visible policing, community safety and coordinated crime prevention efforts throughout the province.

post_title: BMW Announces Global Recall Over Fire Risk
post_content:
n

German carmaker BMW has confirmed a global recall of hundreds of thousands of vehicles due to a potential fire risk linked to faulty engine starters.

nnnn

A company spokesperson told AFP on Wednesday that the recall would affect a “mid-six-figure number” of cars worldwide. BMW will contact affected vehicle owners directly and replace the potentially defective starters.

nnnn

According to a company statement, 16 BMW models fitted with starters produced between July 2020 and July 2022 may be affected. The issue is linked to excessive wear in the electromagnet over time, which could lead to technical failure.

nnnn

“BMW AG recommends that after starting the engine – especially after remote engine start – the vehicle should not be left unattended with the engine running,” the company said.

nnnn

BMW explained that, following customer complaints and vehicle inspections, it was established that the starters in the identified vehicles could become defective. The company also warned that a short circuit in the electromagnet cannot be ruled out, which could cause local overheating.

nnnn

“In the worst case, this can lead to a vehicle fire while driving,” the statement added.

nnnn

The recall was first reported by industry publication kfz-betrieb.

nnnn

This is not the first major recall for BMW in recent years. In 2024, the company was forced to cut its financial outlook after booking losses worth hundreds of millions of euros when it recalled around 1.5 million vehicles over faulty brakes supplied by Continental.

nnnn

However, BMW has indicated that the latest recall is unlikely to have any significant impact on its earnings.

nnnn

Motorists are advised to remain alert for official communication from BMW and to follow safety guidance while the recall process is underway.

post_title: Mpumalanga Lekgotla adopts GBVF action pledge

n

Municipal leaders and partners in Mpumalanga have adopted a bold declaration aimed at accelerating action against Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) while strengthening women’s leadership in local government.

nnnn

The Mpumalanga SALGA Women’s Commission (SWC) Provincial Lekgotla concluded at Premier Hotel The Winkler after a two-day programme held on 10 and 11 February 2026 under the theme: “Letsema: Men, Women, Boys and Girls Working Together to End GBVF.” Delegates included councillors, provincial departments, Chapter 9 institutions, traditional leadership and civil society organisations, with discussions focused on prevention, protection, survivor support and accountability.

nnnn

Opening the gathering, Mpumalanga SWC Provincial Commissioner Cllr S. Makushe-Mazibuko described GBVF as a lived reality across communities and called for a whole-of-government and whole-of-society response. She said the Lekgotla was convened to reflect on SWC work, assess progress on previous resolutions, strengthen Multi-Party Women’s Commissions (MPWCs) as Section 79 committees, improve women’s representation and deepen gender mainstreaming across municipalities.

nnnn

Keynote speaker Cllr S.E. Mgcina, Gauteng SWC Provincial Commissioner, urged leaders to demonstrate courage and coordination, adding that the SWC must drive gender-responsive governance, influence implementation and hold institutions accountable for measurable change.

nnnn

Delegates heard a provincial update on GBVF from Major General D.G. Xaba, who emphasised the need to strengthen policing partnerships and community-based prevention structures working alongside municipalities and traditional leadership.

nnnn

The adopted SWC Declaration commits municipalities to time-bound measures, including stronger multi-sectoral partnerships with SAPS, the Office of the Premier, the Department of Social Development, the Commission for Gender Equality, traditional leadership and NGOs. It also calls for institutionalising the National Strategic Plan on GBVF within local government through gender-responsive planning, budgeting, monitoring and auditing in the 2026/27 municipal cycle.

nnnn

Other resolutions include implementing gender budget classification, prioritising women for senior management roles, expanding mentorship and leadership development, and improving survivor-centred support at first-contact points to reduce secondary victimisation. post_title: Farmers rebuild after devastating floods

nnnn

An oversight visit to three key agricultural projects — the Dingledale Irrigation Scheme, Benica Farms in Acornhoek and Mariti Harvest — highlighted both the scale of the losses and the resilience of local producers. The visit was led by the Mpumalanga MEC for Agriculture, Rural Development, Land and Environmental Affairs, Khethiwe Moeketsi, alongside the municipal executive led by Executive Mayor Lydia Moroane, Council Speaker Ruth Raganya, Chief Whip Malandule, MMC for Economic Development, Environment and Planning Patricia Gubayi, ward councillors and community representatives.

post_title: Crumbling Classrooms Endanger Mzinti Learners

Learners at Mzinti Primary School are attending classes in buildings described as structurally unsafe, raising serious concerns about child safety and the state of school infrastructure in rural areas.

Although the storm did not occur during school hours, the incident has intensified concerns about what could happen if severe weather strikes while learners are in class. Parts of the school are now said to be too unsafe for teaching and learning.

nnnn

Beyond the infrastructure decay, the school is reported to be battling overcrowding, a lack of ICT resources, crime including theft and burglary, insufficient parental support, and shortages of learning and teaching support materials such as desks and chairs.

nnnn

The SGB has formally appealed to the Mpumalanga Department of Education to demolish unsafe structures and replace them with permanent, modern classrooms that are safe, dignified and suitable for learning. Calls have also been made for urgent assessments, decommissioning of dangerous buildings, long-term planning to end overcrowding, and prioritisation of rural schools in infrastructure budgets.

post_title: ARV Tender Turmoil Raises Red Flags
post_content:
n

Health Minister Dr Aaron Motsoaledi has sought to reassure Parliament that disruptions linked to the national antiretroviral (ARV) tender will not derail South Africa’s HIV treatment programme, despite mounting concern over the financial stability of suppliers and a controversial takeover arrangement.

nnnn

The minister briefed MPs after it emerged that two companies awarded contracts to supply ARVs applied for business rescue in 2025. One of those suppliers is now linked to a proposed takeover by Hetero, an India-based pharmaceutical company that has also taken the Department of Health to court over the same tender amid suspicions of price-fixing.

nnnn

Parliamentarians from across parties questioned whether the department had done enough due diligence before awarding contracts, warning that any weakness in the supply chain could place patients at risk. The debate has been sharpened by lingering mistrust following the department’s widely criticised Digital Vibes tender saga, which has made MPs wary of decisions that appear rushed or insufficiently scrutinised.

nnnn

Barrs Pharmaceuticals and Innovata are among seven companies appointed to supply ARVs. MPs indicated discomfort that a supplier under business rescue could shift ownership or control while remaining tied to a key public-health contract — especially when the incoming entity has been involved in litigation linked to that very tender.

nnnn

Motsoaledi told the committee he is not directly involved in tender processes and said the department does not assess the financial statements of companies bidding for contracts. “We cannot examine balance sheets because, for us to do so, we do not have any skill whatsoever,” he said.

nnnn

However, Economic Freedom Fighters MP Naledi Chirwa argued that the minister’s position was misleading, saying the Public Finance Management Act requires the state to satisfy itself that bidders have the financial capacity to deliver. “There are too many red flags for us not to be suspicious with what is happening with this ARV tender,” she said.

nnnn

Health department officials responded that it is the role of National Treasury and the Department of Trade to flag risk indicators in companies’ financial standing and corporate status.

nnnn

Despite the friction, Motsoaledi insisted that medicine availability at state facilities has not been affected. He told MPs that clinics typically maintain a three-month buffer stock, which should cushion patients from short-term shocks while the tender issues are addressed.

nnnn

The committee’s scrutiny is expected to continue, with MPs demanding clearer accountability on vetting processes, supplier stability, and safeguards to protect uninterrupted ARV access.

post_title: Your Pad May Be Disrupting Your Flow
post_content:
n

A new University of the Free State (UFS) study is raising fresh questions about what South Africans may be exposed to during their monthly cycle. Researchers found that every sanitary pad and pantyliner tested contained at least two hormone-disrupting chemicals, including products marketed as “free from harmful chemicals”.

nnnn

Published in Science of the Total Environment, the study analysed 16 brands of sanitary pads and eight types of pantyliners sold in South African retail stores. The team screened for three groups of endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs): phthalates, bisphenols (including BPA), and parabens.

nnnn

The results showed widespread contamination across all products tested. Bisphenols were detected in 100% of pads and 75% of pantyliners, while parabens were found in over 81% of pads and 75% of liners. Phthalates appeared in all pantyliners tested and in 50% of sanitary pads. Researchers said these chemicals may not always be added on purpose, but could migrate into products through plastics, adhesives, inks, and manufacturing processes.

nnnn

What makes this issue especially personal is where these products are used. Menstrual pads and liners come into contact with mucosal tissue, which can absorb chemicals more directly than normal skin. While the amount in a single product might seem small, the study warns that repeated exposure over many years could add up. Long-term exposure to EDCs has been linked in research to hormonal disruption, fertility challenges, endometriosis, and certain cancers.

nnnn

The study also highlights gaps in regulation and transparency. In South Africa, standards focus largely on performance and hygiene, but researchers say there are limited chemical standards for the substances detected, and manufacturers are generally not required to disclose full ingredient lists.

nnnn

For consumers, the advice is practical rather than panic-driven: look for products with independent certification such as OEKO-TEX Standard 100, and consider reusable alternatives where suitable. The UFS team says it is also working on innovations, including reusable pads with antimicrobial properties.

nnnn

Ultimately, the research is a call for clearer labelling, stronger safety standards, and more honest “clean” marketing—so that shoppers can make informed choices about products used month after month, year after year.

Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) MP Sihle Lonzi used Wednesday’s State of the Nation Address (SONA) debate to slam government’s approach to youth unemployment, accusing leaders of blaming young people for a jobs crisis that is structural and deepening.

He pointed specifically to young people placed as education assistants and said some had allegedly not been paid since last year.

nnnn

Beyond criticising existing initiatives, Lonzi called for an economic shift that tackles unemployment at its roots. He argued that South Africa needs faster economic growth and a renewed focus on industrialisation, including bringing factories back to create sustainable employment at scale.

nnnn

His comments come at a time when youth unemployment remains one of the country’s most pressing challenges, with growing frustration among jobseekers who say they are applying repeatedly without success. post_title: Parliament Warns Colleges Over Foreign Hires
post_content:
n

Parliament has issued a stern warning to universities and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) colleges, cautioning institutions against using “internationalisation” as a loophole to sidestep South Africa’s immigration and labour laws when employing foreign nationals.

nnnn

The warning was delivered during a joint meeting of the Portfolio Committee on Higher Education and Training and the Portfolio Committee on Home Affairs, where MPs raised concerns about compliance failures, weak oversight and unreliable data on foreign academic appointments across the post-school education sector. Briefings by the Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) and the Department of Home Affairs reportedly exposed serious gaps in data management and coordination, leaving Parliament unable to properly assess whether institutions are following legal requirements when hiring foreign staff.

nnnn

Higher Education and Training Minister Buti Manamela told the committees that the absence of credible data undermines effective oversight and makes it difficult to determine whether foreign nationals are being appointed to genuinely scarce and critical skills posts, or whether regulations are being bypassed.

nnnn

Committee members stressed that foreign appointments must align strictly with the country’s Critical Skills framework and should not displace suitably qualified South Africans. They warned that institutions must be able to demonstrate clear skills shortages before turning to international recruitment, particularly in roles that are not classified as scarce.

nnnn

Chairperson of the Portfolio Committee on Higher Education and Training, Tebogo Letsie, said compliance is non-negotiable. “When South African students go to other countries, they are expected to follow the laws of those countries. We expect the same from those who come here,” he said, adding that internationalisation must not be used as an excuse to ignore immigration laws.

nnnn

While emphasising that Parliament is not opposed to foreign academics and recognises their contributions in scarce disciplines, MPs expressed alarm over oversight findings that foreign nationals were occupying senior management and administrative posts, including principals and chief financial officers — positions not necessarily linked to critical skills.

nnnn

The Home Affairs committee further warned that employing undocumented foreign nationals is a criminal offence under Section 38 of the Immigration Act, which prohibits employers from hiring foreign nationals without valid work authorisation.

nnnn

The committees said they will intensify oversight, including engagement with the Department of Employment and Labour in the coming weeks, and increased scrutiny once proposed immigration-related legislation is tabled in Parliament.

“The funds go a long way towards ensuring that SANRAL fulfils its mandate of delivering quality road infrastructure that adds value to the lives of South African citizens,” Mona said.

nnnn

He added that the national road network plays a critical role in supporting basic services such as electricity, water, sanitation, telecommunications and public transport, and must meet industrial, commercial and household needs.

nnnn

nnnn

post_title: Hawks Bust Education Corruption Ring

27 officials from the Mpumalanga Department of Education were arrested on Sunday morning, 22 February, during a coordinated anti-corruption sting operation carried out across Mpumalanga, Gauteng, Limpopo and the Western Cape.

nnnn

The arrests form part of a major investigation into a R113 million corruption scheme being pursued by the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation(Hawks). In total, 41 individuals and companies are linked to the case, facing charges of fraud, theft, money laundering and contraventions of the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA).

nnnn

Those detained include nine departmental officials, 14 service providers and four other individuals connected to the alleged scheme. Among the high-profile suspects are the former acting Head of Department (HOD), the former acting Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and chief directors responsible for planning.

nnnnnnnn

Mpumalanga Hawks head, Major General Nico Gerber, said the alleged corruption dates back to 2018. The matter was reported during the 2019/2020 financial year, with a formal criminal case opened in 2020.

nnnn

According to Gerber, officials allegedly fabricated “emergency repair” and maintenance projects at 21 schools across the province. While some limited work may have been done, tenders and invoices were allegedly grossly inflated, procurement processes were bypassed, and service providers were unlawfully handpicked.

nnnn

Investigators further allege that false and inflated invoices were submitted for services purportedly rendered to the department, with financial irregularities stretching back more than five years. Contractors are accused of working in collusion with departmental officials to facilitate the scheme.

nnnn

Hawks spokesperson Magonseni Nkosi described the operation as a major breakthrough in tackling corruption in public institutions.

nnnn

“Following a lengthy investigation into irregularities within the Department of Education in Mpumalanga, we conducted a takedown operation in which 27 suspects were arrested. The operation is ongoing, and we are hopeful that the remaining suspects will be apprehended in due course,” said Nkosi.

nnnn

In a statement issued on 21 February 2026, the Mpumalanga Department of Education confirmed awareness of the Hawks’ operation. The department said the matter is now before the courts and is regarded as sub judice, and therefore declined to comment on the merits of the case.

nnnn

The department reiterated its commitment to ethical governance, transparency and accountability, maintaining a zero-tolerance stance on corruption and maladministration. It further stated that it will cooperate fully with law enforcement agencies to ensure due process is followed.

nnnn

The case is expected to continue in court as investigations expand, with further arrests anticipated as authorities pursue the remaining suspects linked to the corruption network.

post_title: Home Affairs Visa Scam Exposed

The Special Investigating Unit (SIU) has uncovered a large-scale permit and visa racket within the Department of Home Affairs, estimated to have cost the state more than R180 million.

nnnn

Acting on a whistleblower tip-off, investigators discovered that four officials — each earning an estimated monthly salary of about R25,000 — allegedly made millions by selling permits and visas to foreign nationals. Acting SIU Head Leonard Lekgetho said the evidence points to serious weaknesses in border and immigration systems, warning that South Africa’s borders have effectively been compromised. He described the department’s operations as being treated “like a marketplace”.

The investigation further revealed that organised syndicates were working with officials responsible for assessing asylum seeker applications. Following a 2024 raid on five refugee reception centres, during which laptops and mobile devices were seized, the SIU found evidence that favourable application outcomes were being sold for between R500 and R3,000.

nnnn

“The SIU investigation revealed that certain officials turned the permit system into a marketplace,” Lekgetho said. “Their modus operandi was simple: applications were sent via WhatsApp for expedited approval, and once approved, money flowed almost immediately.”

nnnn

The findings expose deep-rooted corruption within the immigration system and raise serious concerns about national security, border control and the integrity of asylum and permit processes in South Africa.

post_title: Billions Lost on Repeating Grades
post_content:
n

The Department of Basic Education (DBE) has revealed that repeating school grades is draining billions of rands from the education budget — funds that many experts say could be better spent on improving early literacy and learning.  

nnnn

According to the Funda Uphumelele National Survey, a major national study into reading outcomes for learners in grades 1 to 4, up to 8 % of the DBE’s budget — around R20 billion — is being used to fund the repetition of learners who fail to meet expected outcomes.  

nnnn

The same report highlights a troubling literacy picture in South African schools:

nnnn

• 15 % of Grade 3 learners scored zero on reading assessments, meaning they could not decode even a single word by the end of their third year of schooling.  

nnnn

• Only around 30 % to 31 % of learners in grades 1 to 3 are reading at the expected level in their home languages, according to the survey results.  

nnnn

These figures underline a foundational problem: many pupils enter schooling without strong reading skills, which affects their ability to succeed in later grades.

nnnn

Research in the report suggests that repeating learners in Grade 1 can lead to temporary learning gains. However, these improvements tend to fade as pupils move up through the system.  

nnnn

Experts argue that spending such large sums on repetition isn’t the most effective way to improve learning outcomes — especially when many of the problems begin in the earliest years of schooling.

nnnn

Educational researchers and advocates are calling for a shift in how the funds are used. They recommend:

nnnn

• Investing more in Early Childhood Development (ECD) so children start school better prepared.  

nnnn

• Introducing structured reading programmes in the early grades, which have been shown to deliver more lasting improvements than repeating learners.  

nnnn

The evidence suggests that focusing on early learning and literacy could reduce the need for repetition in the first place — breaking a costly cycle and giving learners a stronger start in their education.

nnnn

Redirecting funds from repetition toward ECD and structured reading programmes might help more children build essential skills from the beginning of their schooling journey.  

nnnn

Education experts warn that unless funding shifts towards effective early literacy support, the cycle of poor reading outcomes and expensive grade repetition may continue.

nnnn

Houses attract snakes because they provide perfect conditions for their prey. Watered gardens and ponds draw frogs, rodents are fond of walls and rockeries, and lizards find hiding spots in human environments. Experts advise residents to remember that snakes do not see houses as foreign — to them, it’s just another part of their habitat.

nnnn

Residents are urged to stay vigilant, secure poultry enclosures, and contact trained handlers when snakes appear indoors.
